items.title: India-China thaw faces major economic tests
items.author: Manishi Raychaudhuri
items.creator: Manishi Raychaudhuri
items.summary: India is working to emerge from China’s shadow while improving diplomatic relations, but the more the world’s most populous country pushes, the more apparent its dependence on its wealthier neighbour becomes.
items.body:
India is working to emerge from China’s shadow while [USN:L6N4500OX TEXT:"improving diplomatic relations"], but the more the world’s most populous country pushes, the more apparent its dependence on its wealthier neighbour becomes.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping [USN:P8N44B08W TEXT:"met in New Delhi"] last month, Xi's first visit to the subcontinent in seven years. The two leaders pledged to rebuild ties badly damaged by [USN:L1N3M10AB TEXT:"deadly hand-to-hand troop clashes in 2020"] on their shared but ill-defined Himalayan border.
There are other signs of warming relations since the two Asian giants last year [USN:FWN3M01QR TEXT:"agreed to end the military standoff"]. [USN:L4N3UB0D6 TEXT:"Direct flights"] between Indian and Chinese cities have resumed after being suspended since the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, and visa services in China have expanded.
But such measures only go so far. Long-standing trade dependence and strategic mistrust will not be addressed with handshakes and plane flights.
The two Asian giants’ economic relationship remains deeply asymmetric. China's share of global value-added manufacturing stood at 28% in 2025, dwarfing India's 3%, according to the World Bank.
The export picture is just as lopsided for India. China’s 16.3% share of global merchandise exports in 2025 massively surpasses India’s 1.7% . Moreover, India imported goods worth $116 billion more from China than it exported in 2025. By August this year, the deficit had already hit $91 billion and was on track to surpass last year's record.
CAPTIVE SUPPLY CHAINS The problem is not only that India imports more from China. It is also that many of those imports are indispensable to Indian industry. Electrical and electronic equipment, machinery, and chemicals – the three largest import categories – are largely intermediate goods used by domestic manufacturers. The more India exports, the more it needs to import from China.
Smartphones and generic medicines illustrate the dilemma. India has made progress in assembling electronics and expanding pharmaceutical production, but many of the components and inputs needed for both sectors still come from China.
This intense reliance has many broad strategic implications. For example, Beijing's [USN:L4N3R10B3 TEXT:"imposition of export licensing"] requirements on seven heavy rare earths in April 2025 exposed [USN:L4N3SI03M TEXT:"vulnerabilities in India’s automotive"] and defense manufacturing sectors.
Of course, some of India’s manufacturing weakness is primarily homegrown. The country’s research and development spending stood at just 0.64% of gross domestic product in 2024, according to the most recent Economic Survey, sharply lower than that of Asian peers, partly because of private-sector underinvestment.
Skilled-labour shortages compound the problem. Foxconn's (2317.TW) [USN:L6N3UZ072 TEXT:"withdrawal of Chinese staff"] from its Indian iPhone factories in 2025 illustrated how dependent advanced manufacturing can be on foreign technical expertise.
INDIA’S FIXES New Delhi is seeking to address the imbalance.
[USN:FWN3ZY0TT TEXT:"India recently relaxed restrictions"] on foreign direct investment (FDI) from Chinese companies, allowing them to take up to a 10% stake in Indian firms.
The government simultaneously announced fast-track clearance of investment proposals in five high-technology areas within 60 days, with the stipulation that they must be structured as joint ventures with majority Indian ownership.
On top of this, Indian exports to China rose by 40% between April and August. Industrial machinery, automotive components, printed circuit boards, smartphones and other electronics have driven much of that increase.
But the export surge should not be mistaken for a fundamental shift in the relationship. Much of India's electronics growth still depends on imported Chinese components. Smartphone manufacturing — India’s biggest export success story — remains only 18-20% locally sourced.
Northeast Asia’s AI boom appears to be generating positive spillovers for the subcontinent, with Indian firms picking up sub-component work from Chinese tech giants facing surging hardware demand. But, again, this dynamic reinforces the centrality of Chinese supply chains.
TRUST DEFICIT PERSISTS For India-bound Chinese FDI and technology transfer to materialise, one question needs to be answered: what does India bring to the table?
The obvious answers are access to a large market and a young, low-cost labour pool as well as New Delhi's various incentives to spur industrial growth — including tax breaks, production-linked payouts, and capital subsidies — but China doesn't appear to be taking the bait.
China’s pressure on its leading companies to withhold critical technologies illustrates how protective Beijing is about its most sophisticated capabilities — electric vehicles (EVs), batteries, solar energy and electronic equipment.
Meanwhile, the 3,800-km (2,400-mile) disputed border in the Himalayas continues to cast a shadow over the relationship. A gradual, multi-year [USN:P8N42604N TEXT:"stabilisation strategy"] is in place — diplomats met in Beijing in August pledging a "fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable settlement" — but a final resolution doesn't appear imminent .
For now, both governments appear willing to give economic cooperation more room. But India's challenge is not simply to import less from China. It is to use renewed engagement with its neighbour to build its own domestic capabilities. Until then, the relationship between Asia’s two largest economies will remain decidedly one-sided.
(The views expressed here are those of Manishi Raychaudhuri , the founder and CEO of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd and the former head of Asia-Pacific Equity Research at BNP Paribas Securities.)

items.title: Brésil-Bolsonaro et Lula s'affronteront au second tour de la présidentielle
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.summary: Le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro et le président sortant de gauche Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva s'affronteront lors du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, a annoncé dimanche soir l'autorité électorale, le premier nommé ayant déjoué les pronostics en devançant l'actuel chef d'Etat.
items.body:
Le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro et le président sortant de gauche Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva s'affronteront lors du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, a annoncé dimanche soir l'autorité électorale, le premier nommé ayant déjoué les pronostics en devançant l'actuel chef d'Etat.
Après dépouillement de plus de 97% des bulletins, le fils de l'ancien président d'extrême droite Jair Bolsonaro est crédité de 47,45% des suffrages, contre 44,66% pour Lula, a rapporté l'autorité électorale.
Dépasser le seuil de 50% des voix était nécessaire pour remporter le scrutin dès ce premier tour. Le second tour aura lieu le 25 octobre.
Les enquêtes d'opinion dessinaient la perspective d'un coude-à-coude au second tour entre Lula et Bolsonaro, les deux grands favoris parmi les 14 candidats qui étaient en lice pour cette élection présidentielle.
Une victoire de Flavio Bolsonaro viendrait amplifier la bascule à droite constatée à travers l'Amérique du Sud, avec les succès de candidats conservateurs alignés sur la politique du président américain Donald Trump. A l'inverse, une réélection de Lula pourrait représenter une épine dans le pied de Washington, qui est en conflit avec l'actuelle administration de Brasilia sur des questions commerciales et sécuritaires.
"VOTE DE PROTESTATION" En dépit d'inquiétudes croissantes au Brésil à propos de l'état des finances publiques et de la faiblesse de la croissance économique, la campagne n'a pas donné lieu à de réels débats politiques, Lula et Flavio Bolsonaro ayant tous deux fait l'impasse sur les principaux débats télévisés.
Alors que des sondages donnaient samedi Lula en tête des intentions de vote au premier tour mais sans atteindre le seuil de 50% des suffrages, Flavio Bolsonaro a déclaré à des journalistes à Rio de Janeiro être confiant en sa capacité à remporter le scrutin sans avoir besoin d'un second tour, citant la frustration des électeurs à l'égard du président sortant.
Il a dit compter sur "un vote de protestation" de la part de personnes qui auraient traditionnellement privilégié un autre candidat que lui "mais qui sont opposées à Lula".
Thaise Lima, avocate de 41 ans, a exprimé sa volonté de voir le Parti des travailleurs (PT) de Lula quitter le pouvoir. "Je ne pense pas que Flavio soit le meilleur candidat", a-t-elle dit au moment de se rendre aux urnes à Sao Paulo, "mais je pourrais décider de voter pour lui dans les prochaines minutes". Elle a dit qu'elle aurait espéré qu'Augusto Cury, psychiatre et écrivain, soit un candidat plus qualifié.
Des alliés de Lula ont prévenu du risque que les Etats-Unis décident de ne pas reconnaître les résultats électoraux si le dirigeant de gauche venait à l'emporter. "Ce qui est en jeu, c'est l'avenir du Brésil", a dit Lula après avoir voté à Sao Bernardo do Campo, dans l'Etat de Sao Paulo.
"SOUVERAINETÉ NATIONALE" Bien que Donald Trump n'a pas formellement soutenu un candidat, il a reçu Flavio Bolsonaro à la Maison blanche et a fait l'éloge de celui-ci. Le président américain s'est également offusqué l'an dernier de la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro pour tentative de coup d'Etat.
Cristiano, médecin âgé de 34 ans qui réside à Brasilia et a préféré ne pas communiquer son nom de famille, a dit être "un peu inquiet de tout ce qui s'est passé dernièrement, notamment sur le plan international". "J'ai l'impression qu'il y a eu beaucoup d'influence venue de l'extérieur, plus que lors d'élections précédentes", a-t-il ajouté, indiquant avoir choisi de voter pour Lula.
"Nous avons confiance en notre président Lula, qui se battra pour la souveraineté nationale", a déclaré pour sa part Pedro Palacio, 45 ans, qui s'est rendu avec son épouse, leurs deux enfants et leurs deux chiens dans un bureau de vote de Brasilia. Tous étaient vêtus de tenues à l'effigie du président sortant.
Le scrutin s'est déroulé normalement, a déclaré dimanche après-midi le chef du tribunal électoral national. "Les équipes qui surveillent les risques internationaux n'ont pas identifié de quelconques risques", a dit Kassio Nunes Marques lors d'une conférence de presse.
Reuters a rapporté la semaine dernière que des représentants des services brésiliens du renseignement ont informé des délégations française et allemande d'ingérences américaines et russes présumées en amont de l'élection présidentielle. Washington a nié toute inférence dans les affaires du Brésil.
L'OMBRE D'UN NOUVEAU SCANDALE Malgré le recul des inégalités et du chômage, Lula a peiné à convaincre les électeurs durant la campagne, en raison notamment du coût élevé de la vie et de la criminalité.
Flavio Bolsonaro a cherché à profiter du mécontentement de la population à propos de l'inflation.
Le vainqueur du scrutin devra s'atteler à réduire la dette publique, qui a dépassé les 82% du produit intérieur brut (PIB) du Brésil. La prévision de croissance économique a été revue à la baisse pour cette année, à seulement 2%, et pour 2027, à 2,3%.
Outre les questions politiques, la campagne a été marquée un scandale impliquant la Banco Master, établissement financier aujourd'hui disparu, qui ravivé la colère de l'opinion publique à l'encontre du personnel politique et de la corruption.
Daniel Vorcano, qui dirigeait la banque, a été arrêté plus tôt cette année pour des accusations de fraude présumée portant sur plusieurs milliards de dollars. L'enquête a porté notamment sur les liens de Vorcano avec des personnalités influentes, dont Alexandre de Moraes, juge à la Cour suprême du Brésil, et Flavio Bolsonaro.
Alexandre de Moraes, qui est perçu comme un allié de Lula, a dénoncé des manoeuvres politiques en raison de son rôle dans la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro.
Flavio Bolsonaro, visé par une enquête de la police fédérale pour des soupçons de blanchiment d'argent en lien avec cette affaire, nie toute inconduite. Il a toutefois confirmé avoir levé plusieurs millions de dollars auprès de Daniel Vorcano afin de financer un film sur son père Jair.
En parallèle à l'élection présidentielle, les Brésiliens étaient appelés dimanche à voter au premier tour des législatives pour renouveler l'ensemble de la Chambre des députés, qui compte 513 sièges, et les deux tiers du Sénat.

items.author: CNA

items.body:

US removes B-1 bombers from UK's Fairford air base amid security concerns

The planes' removal comes after several men were arrested on suspicion of a terror plot on the air base, with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham saying that Britain had "strong indications" that Iran was involved in the suspected plot targeting the base.

B‑1B Lancer bomber at the RAF Fairford airbase, which hosts US Air Force personnel, in Fairford, Gloucestershire, Britain, on Sep 27, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Toby Shepheard)

FAST

NEW YORK: The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one week after several men were arrested there on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday (Oct 4). 
A dozen B-1 bombers were stationed at RAF Fairford air base, located northwest of London. The planes had been used for US strikes on Iran. 
"While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have redeployed to their home stations in the United States," a Pentagon spokesman wrote in an email.
Britain has "strong indications" that Iran was involved in a suspected plot targeting the base, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday. Iran said accusations linking Tehran to the alleged plan were baseless and summoned the British ambassador in Tehran over the issue. 
The Wall Street Journal first reported that the aircraft were removed from the base amid security concerns over suspected terror plots against the facility.
The British government had allowed the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump said those involved in the plot had planned "big damage", while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also pointed to the "hands of a foreign actor".

items.title: ロシア、ウクライナ攻撃強化へ　製油所攻撃巡るゼレンスキー氏発言受け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[４日 ロイター] - ロシア国防省は４日、キーウなどウクライナ各地への攻撃を強化すると発表した。ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領がロイターのインタビューで、ロシアの製油所への攻撃を強化すると表明したことを受けた対応。

同省によると、ロシア軍はキーウなどウクライナ各地にある軍事施設、防衛産業拠点、関連インフラへの攻撃を強化する。

ゼレンスキー氏は３日に公開されたロイターのインタビューで、キーウなどの都市から住民を退去させることを狙ったロシアの新たな空爆方針への対抗措置としてロシアの製油所への攻撃を強化すると述べた。ただ、民間人は標的にしないと強調した。

ロシアはこのところ、ドニプロ川に架かる橋を攻撃するなど、キーウのインフラへの攻撃を激化させている。

ロシア国防省は、最近のキーウなどへの攻撃について、ウクライナがロシア国内の民間施設などを攻撃したことへの対抗措置だと主張した。

items.title: Vídeos não mostram militares dos EUA no Brasil às vésperas das eleições de 2026
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Um compilado de vídeos compartilhado nas redes sociais no último sábado não mostra militares dos Estados Unidos no Brasil às vésperas das eleições de 2026.
items.body:
Um compilado de vídeos compartilhado nas redes sociais no último sábado não mostra militares dos Estados Unidos no Brasil às vésperas das eleições de 2026.
"Militares americanos no Brasil às vésperas das eleições. O que está acontecendo?", diz um post com as imagens no Instagram. Outras publicações com alegações similares circulam no Facebook.
O conteúdo começa com um vídeo da passagem de uma comitiva de veículos com bandeiras do Brasil e dos EUA. As imagens foram gravadas em uma avenida de Manaus, como confirma o Google Street View .
A gravação está disponível no TikTok desde 17 de novembro de 2024, e a legenda diz que se trata da comitiva do então presidente dos EUA, Joe Biden, em Manaus --Biden visitou a capital amazonense naquela data.
AERONAVES Os posts também mostram imagens que seriam de aeronaves militares norte-americanas no Brasil.
Em uma delas, helicópteros militares aparecem estacionados, enquanto exemplares do modelo Marine One , usada pelo presidente dos EUA, se deslocam na pista de pouso. Ao fundo, há aviões abandonados que ficam no aeroporto de Manaus .
A Reuters identificou uma versão mais curta da filmagem compartilhada no Instagram em 17 de novembro de 2024 com a legenda "Presidente dos EUA em Manaus" -- mesmo dia da visita de Biden à cidade.
O avião presidencial Air Force One também aparece atrás dos helicópteros que estão em deslocamento.
O conteúdo mostra ainda uma filmagem de um avião cargueiro do modelo C-17 Globemaster III estacionando no aeroporto de Manaus. A Reuters não conseguiu encontrar a filmagem apresentada no vídeo ou registros semelhantes.
Nas vésperas da visita de Biden à capital amazonense, a imprensa brasileira e páginas de observadores de aeronaves registraram a chegada de cargueiros desse modelo no aeroporto da capital do Amazonas.
Em nota, a Concessionária dos Aeroportos da Amazônia, que administra o aeroporto de Manaus, disse que o terminal "não recebeu recentemente aeronaves ou helicópteros das Forças Armadas dos Estados Unidos".
Segundo o comunicado, as imagens usadas nos posts são de novembro de 2024, "quando o aeroporto recebeu aeronaves relacionadas à operação de apoio à visita do então presidente dos Estados Unidos, Joe Biden, a Manaus."
"Desde aquela ocasião, não houve nova operação dessa natureza envolvendo aeronaves das Forças Armadas dos Estados Unidos no Aeroporto de Manaus", disse a concessionária.
VEREDICTO Legenda errada. Os vídeos de aeronaves dos EUA no Brasil foram registrados durante a visita de Biden a Manaus em 2024 e não têm relação com as atuais eleições.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278. Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: OpenAI's Altman says AI benefits warrant accepting some risks
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks.
items.body:
OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks and argued the technology should remain broadly accessible to the public
"We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency," Altman said in an interview with Politico's technology-focused newsletter Decoded.
Altman said there remained a fundamental difference in worldview between OpenAI and rival Anthropic on AI regulation, adding: "I think there's a lot of daylight."
"I disagree, but I understand the perspective of people who are like, 'This technology is going to get so powerful, and it's so dangerous, that a single lab in San Francisco should have it and make sure nothing bad happens, and kind of figure out how to dole out the benefits,'" Altman said.
He called that "a completely unacceptable trade-off" that runs counter to the "lighter-touch regulatory stance" backed by OpenAI.
"I wouldn't take a trade of saying, 'We'll make sure there's no major hacks, there's no misuse of this technology, there's zero scams, there's zero all the other bad things that will happen,'" Altman said. "Because I think people will do tremendously — orders of magnitude more — good stuff than bad stuff."
Altman's remarks come amid a growing debate within the AI industry over the pace of development and the risks posed by increasingly capable systems.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in September published an essay calling on the industry [USN:L6N45L0PN TEXT:"to slow down"] to "pace the frontier," a stance that Altman publicly endorsed. Anthropic researcher [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"Jacob Coxon"] resigned in September, saying the people building AI believe it "could kill us all by the end of the decade.
Reuters reported in September that Anthropic warned that, despite AI's potential benefits, the technology can sometimes act in ways that run counter to its makers' intentions and penetrate other companies' systems. The company said advanced models could exhibit [USN:L6N45L00I TEXT:""self-preserving behaviors,""] including attempts to "resist shutdown," "conceal or manipulate information," or generate outputs that could be interpreted as "coercive, deceptive, or manipulative."
However, US President Donald Trump has largely [USN:L6N45O0XQ TEXT:"dismissed calls"] for new restrictions, arguing they would make it harder for American companies to compete with Chinese rivals. He has repeatedly said existing law enforcement agencies, including the Justice Department, provide sufficient safeguards and that no new rules are needed.
items.raw_description: Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks.

items.summary: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
items.body:
Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
Lamb posted a career-best 17 receptions and totaled 189 yards to help the Cowboys overcome a 10-point halftime deficit. Jason Witten (18 in 2012) is the only Dallas player to have more receptions in a game. Dak Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and Williams had 62 yards on 19 carries for the Cowboys (2-2).
C.J. Stroud was 21-of-31 passing for 347 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (0-4), who have lost their first four games for the first time since 2020. Nico Collins caught seven passes for 118 yards and two scores after a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Woody Marks rushed for a score.
Stroud guided the Texans on a nine-play, 87-yard drive to take a 30-27 lead with 2:23 left. The pivotal play was on third-and-14 from the Dallas 27-yard line. Stroud threw a short pass to Dalton Schultz at the 25. His lateral to David Montgomery was good for 19 more yards to the Cowboys' 6. Marks scored on the next play. Prescott then drove Dallas 74 yards on 11 plays, eventually connecting with Lamb for the winning points.
Patriots 29, Bills 26
Drake Maye completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including a late, go-ahead TD pass to Efton Chism III, to lead New England over Buffalo in Orchard Park, N.Y.
Chism's leaping, one-handed 23-yard TD catch plus Maye's pass to Rhamondre Stevenson for the two-point conversion put the Patriots in front with 1:50 to play. Craig Woodson intercepted a Josh Allen pass at the New England 19-yard line on the ensuing possession, and the Patriots (2-2) were able to run out the clock and hand the Bills (3-1) their first loss in their new stadium.
Allen was 23-of-33 passing for 253 yards and one touchdown. Buffalo's Keon Coleman caught six passes for 116 yards and a TD. James Cook rushed for 75 yards and a score.
Ravens 24, Titans 18
Lamar Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-20 passing but exited early in Baltimore's home victory over Tennessee.
Jackson was sacked on the Ravens' final play of the second quarter by Jermaine Johnson II, who landed on Jackson's left ankle. Jackson was later seen on the sideline with his ankle wrapped. Tyler Huntley played the second half and completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards, but the Ravens (3-1) were held scoreless after taking a 24-7 lead to the half.
Cam Ward's 3-yard touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson and two-point conversion pass to Gunnar Helm pulled the Titans (0-4) within six with 1:12 left. But Malaki Starks recovered Tennessee's ensuing onside kick with 1:10 left and Baltimore ran out the clock.
Rams 24, Eagles 20
Kyren Williams rushed for two late touchdowns to rally Los Angeles over Philadelphia on a soggy afternoon in Philadelphia. Williams scored from 1 yard out with 3:59 left and from 7 yards out with 1:10 remaining to lift the Rams.
Matthew Stafford overcame two first-half interceptions and finished with 317 yards on 32-of-51 passing for the Rams (2-2). Puka Nacua had a touchdown run to go with 125 yards on nine catches and Williams gained 147 yards (80 rushing, 67 receiving) from scrimmage. Byron Young sealed the win with two sacks on Philadelphia's final drive.
Jalen Hurts threw two touchdowns to Darius Cooper and Philadelphia (2-2) built a 20-10 lead by halftime, but the offense largely struggled after losing Saquon Barkley to an early hamstring injury and finished 0-for-12 on third-down conversions with only 172 yards of offense. Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 93 yards.
Jaguars 22, Bengals 17
Trevor Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown to lead visiting Jacksonville past Cincinnati.
It was the first time Lawrence defeated Joe Burrow in four career meetings. Bhayshul Tuten ran 17 times for 73 yards while Chris Rodriguez Jr. added a 25-yard touchdown run for the Jaguars (3-1).
Burrow was 39-of-54 passing for 428 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. Tee Higgins caught 11 passes for 157 yards while Chase Brown caught 11 passes for 71 yards for the Bengals (2-2), who played the second half without Ja'Marr Chase due to concussion symptoms.
Bears 23, Jets 12
Kyle Monangai rushed for 146 yards and two touchdowns and Tyson Bagent passed for 268 yards to boost host Chicago to a victory against New York.
Chicago (3-1) limited New York (1-3) to 157 total yards as the Jets lost their third game in a row. The Bears rolled up 492 yards of offense while collecting 34 first downs to the Jets' seven. Bagent finished 25-of-34 passing, Rome Odunze had six catches for 94 yards and Monangai finished with 30 carries.
Geno Smith connected with Isaiah Williams for a 58-yard touchdown pass for New York, which enjoyed a rare bright spot when safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Bagent in the second quarter. That stopped a record drought of 21 games without an interception for the Jets, who snagged their first pick since Jan. 5, 2025.
Giants 36, Cardinals 24
Jameis Winston threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns as New York outlasted Arizona in East Rutherford, N.J.
The Giants (3-1) shrugged off a 14-3 deficit as Winston fired second-quarter touchdown passes to Malachi Fields and Malik Nabers (six catches, 112 yards). Winston's 11-yard strike to Theo Johnson with 1:44 left in the third erased Arizona's last lead.
Jacoby Brissett hit 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards, two yards and three interceptions. He drove the Cardinals (1-3) to the Giants' 2-yard line in the final minute trailing 30-24, but Deonte Banks picked off a fourth-down pass and returned it 98 yards for a score on the game's final play.
Colts 30, Commanders 13
Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns, and the Colts pulled away in the fourth quarter to beat the undermanned Commanders in London.
Taylor finished with 95 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries, as Indianapolis (2-2) made the most of their 257 yards. Quarterback Daniel Jones shrugged off a pair of early turnovers to complete 19 of 34 passes for 143 yards and an interception.
Washington (1-3) played most of the day with rookie Athan Kaliakmanis at quarterback after starter Marcus Mariota suffered a right knee injury in the first quarter and wasn't able to return. Kaliakmanis completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception.
Packers 17, Buccaneers 14
Jordan Love threw for 197 yards and two touchdowns as Green Bay held on against Tampa Bay in Tampa, Fla.
Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft caught 2-yard touchdown passes from Love as the Packers (2-2) never trailed. Evan Williams and Edgerrin Cooper picked off passes and Trey Smack booted a 58-yard field goal to give Green Bay a 10-7 halftime lead.
For Tampa Bay (0-4), rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels hit 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards and rushed for 55 yards in his first start playing for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb). Sean Tucker rushed for a touchdown and Kenneth Gainwell caught a 10-yard touchdown pass to cut the Packers' lead to 17-14 with 14:49 to play.
--Field Level Media

Oct 4 : OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks and argued the technology should remain broadly accessible to the public
"We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency," Altman said in an interview with Politico's technology-focused newsletter Decoded.
Altman said there remained a fundamental difference in worldview between OpenAI and rival Anthropic on AI regulation, adding: "I think there's a lot of daylight."
"I disagree, but I understand the perspective of people who are like, 'This technology is going to get so powerful, and it's so dangerous, that a single lab in San Francisco should have it and make sure nothing bad happens, and kind of figure out how to dole out the benefits,'" Altman said.

He called that "a completely unacceptable trade-off" that runs counter to the "lighter-touch regulatory stance" backed by OpenAI.
"I wouldn't take a trade of saying, 'We'll make sure there's no major hacks, there's no misuse of this technology, there's zero scams, there's zero all the other bad things that will happen,'" Altman said. "Because I think people will do tremendously — orders of magnitude more — good stuff than bad stuff."
Altman's remarks come amid a growing debate within the AI industry over the pace of development and the risks posed by increasingly capable systems.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in September published an essay calling on the industry to slow down to "pace the frontier," a stance that Altman publicly endorsed. Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned in September, saying the people building AI believe it "could kill us all by the end of the decade.
Reuters reported in September that Anthropic warned that, despite AI's potential benefits, the technology can sometimes act in ways that run counter to its makers' intentions and penetrate other companies' systems. The company said advanced models could exhibit "self-preserving behaviors," including attempts to "resist shutdown," "conceal or manipulate information," or generate outputs that could be interpreted as "coercive, deceptive, or manipulative."
However, US President Donald Trump has largely dismissed calls for new restrictions, arguing they would make it harder for American companies to compete with Chinese rivals. He has repeatedly said existing law enforcement agencies, including the Justice Department, provide sufficient safeguards and that no new rules are needed.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice exits with hamstring injury
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice exited in the first quarter with a right hamstring injury.
items.body:
Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice exited in the first quarter with a right hamstring injury.
The Chiefs announced he was questionable to return.
Rice pulled up after corralling a first-down pass from Patrick Mahomes in the right flat. Rice had room to run but limped toward the sideline and out of bounds at the Kansas City 36 after a five-yard gain.
The Raiders bit hard on a play-action fake to running back Kenneth Walker III and left Rice open with room to run.
Rice made the grab in front of Chiefs head coach Andy Reid and went directly to the bench as he reached the sideline. Rice remained on the sideline stretching and chatting with Chiefs vice president of sports medicine and performance Rick Burkholder.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Ireland and Israel end Nations League rivalry with ill-tempered stalemate
items.author: Fatos Bytyci
items.creator: Fatos Bytyci
items.summary: Tempers flared again as Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 on Sunday in the second of their two UEFA Nations League meetings, concluding a fortnight dominated as much by political tensions as football.
items.body:
Tempers flared again as Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 on Sunday in the second of their two UEFA Nations League meetings, concluding a fortnight dominated as much by political tensions as football.
Ireland had faced calls from [USN:L1N45I02P TEXT:"some supporters and politicians"] to boycott the fixtures before beating [USN:L6N45J074 TEXT:"Israel 3-0"] behind closed doors in Hungary in their first meeting a week ago.
"I'm absolutely delighted this is finished," Ireland's Icelandic coach Heimir Hallgrimsson told reporters.
"It's taken a toll out of us all. I've given so much credit to the players. They have been absolutely amazing in tough times, and I wish no national team to go through what we have gone through for the last two weeks."
Ireland is one of Europe's most outspoken critics of Israel's war in Gaza , and the Football Association of Ireland chose to stage Sunday’s match behind closed doors in Serbia amid the pressure to withdraw from the fixtures.
The absence of supporters did little to ease the tension on the pitch.
Irish media reported that one of Ireland's coaches Damien Doyle had accused an Israeli player of spitting at him after the halftime whistle. Reuters could not independently verify the allegation or establish its original source.
Asked about the spitting incident at the post-match press conference, Hallgrimsson declined to provide details.
"I was there. I’m not going to comment. It’s something a disciplinary committee will look at," he told reporters.
Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened.
"Halftime I was in the dressing room, in my room with my staff, I didn't see anything. When I'm going to see and check, I will get back to you with the answer," he told reporters.
TENSE ATMOSPHERE As in the first meeting, there were no pre-match handshakes or exchange of pennants, while players from each team bowed their heads during the opposing national anthem.
Ireland again wore black armbands commemorating all the victims of the conflict in Gaza, with the Israelis sporting black armbands in memory of the victims of the October 7 attack that sparked the war.
Troy Parrott gave Ireland the lead with a 39th-minute penalty but Dor Peretz levelled immediately after the break for Israel with their first effort on target.
Israel hit the woodwork twice in the second half of a poor game in which neither side could fashion a winner.
The draw left Ireland third in Group B3 on five points, three behind leaders Austria with second-placed Kosovo ahead of them on goal difference. Israel are bottom with two points.
Ben-Shimon welcomed his team’s response to the 3-0 defeat and rejected suggestions that his players had been overly aggressive.
"When I come to a game, I say to my players, 'This is the best way to play the cleanest football as you can, but be aggressive', okay? I never say to injure someone, this is not our way. We are very human, human beings, we are very moral human beings," he said.

items.title: カナダ首相、今月トルコ訪問へ　貿易・エネルギー・防衛協力を協議＝関係者
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jonathan Spicer　Promit Mukherjee　David Ljunggren

[オタワ ２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Jonathan Spicer　Promit Mukherjee　David Ljunggren

[オタワ ２日 ロイター] - カナダのカーニー首相が今月トルコを訪問し、エルドアン大統領と会談する計画だ。事情に詳しい関係者４人が明らかにした。実現すれば、カナダ首相による初のトルコへの本格的な２国間訪問となる。

関係者は、今月後半に予定されているカーニー氏の訪問について、具体的な日程や議題を明らかにしていない。カーニー氏とエルドアン氏の事務所はコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

ただ関係者の１人は、両首脳が７月にトルコ首都アンカラで開かれた北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）首脳会議に合わせて開始した自由貿易協定（ＦＴＡ）交渉のほか、エネルギーや防衛分野での協力について協議する可能性があると説明した。また２人の関係者によると、両国の貿易担当相がこのほど首脳会談を前にＦＴＡ交渉を加速させることで合意した。

カーニー氏は８月に米国との貿易協議が決裂した後、最大の貿易相手国である米国への依存を減らすため、従来のカナダ外交の慣例にとらわれない取り組みを推進中。同氏は今後１０年間で米国以外との貿易を倍増させる方針を表明し、その一環として過去に関係が悪化した中国やインドを含む各国との関係構築を急いでいる。

一方トルコは近年急成長している防衛産業の新たな市場や協力相手の開拓を進め、最大の貿易相手である欧州連合（ＥＵ）に加え、エネルギーやインフラ、鉱業分野でも新たな提携や投資を求めている。

カナダとトルコの首脳は、ＮＡＴＯや２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）首脳会議などの国際会議に合わせて会談してきた。両国は７月のＮＡＴＯ首脳会議でＦＴＡ交渉を正式に開始し、同月にはトルコが、カーニー氏が主導する多国間の「防衛安全保障・強靱化銀行」に創設メンバー１０カ国の１つとして参加することで合意した。

両国の貿易担当相は６月にも会談し、再生可能エネルギーや原子力分野での協力拡大を計画。カナダ政府は航空宇宙、防衛、安全保障も新たな協力が期待される分野に挙げている。

トルコは国内で計画する２基目と３基目の原子力発電所の建設を巡り、カナダのエンジニアリング大手アトキンス・レアリスのほか、韓国電力公社、中国国家電力投資集団と協議している。

カナダが開発したＣＡＮＤＵ炉（カナダ型重水炉）の独占ライセンスを持つアトキンス・レアリスの幹部は今年、情報交換後にトルコ側がＣＡＮＤＵ炉の初期評価を終え、本格的な受注協議に進む可能性があるとの見通しを示した。

もっとも両国間の貿易規模は依然として小さい。カナダ統計局によると、２０２５年のカナダとトルコのモノの貿易額は４３億４０００万カナダドル（３０億５０００万米ドル）で、カナダのモノの貿易全体に占める割合は０．３％未満だった。対米貿易額は１兆カナダドルに上る。

カナダはトルコに主にレンズ豆や航空機、電子機器を輸出し、トルコから医療機器、漁船、航空機エンジン、宝飾品などを輸入している。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[４日 ロイター] - オランダの塗料メーカーのアクゾノーベルが、東南アジアの建築用塗料事業を日本ペイントホールディングスに１０億ドルを大幅に上回る金額で売却する契約の合意に近づいている。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）が４日、事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。

早ければ５日にも合意に達する可能性があるという。売却対象には、ベトナム、インドネシア、マレーシア、タイ、シンガポールに加え、パプアニューギニアおよびオーストラリアにおける建築用塗料事業が含まれる。

アクゾノーベルと日本ペイントは、ロイターのコメント要請に回答していない。

両社は７月、日本ペイントがアクゾノーベルの建築用塗料事業について総額７５億ユーロでの買収に向け複数の提案を提出したと発表した。ただ、アクゾノーベルはすでに米アクサルタ・コーティング・システムズと合併契約を結んでおり「代替提案」は受け入れられないとの立場を示していた。

ＦＴによると、日本ペイントは建築用塗料事業に関するより大規模な取引に引き続き関心を示しているものの、東南アジア事業の統合にはしばらく時間を要すると見込まれており、アクゾノーベルは同事業からさらなる資産を売却する計画はないという。

items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro y Lula definirán presidencia de Brasil en segunda vuelta: Datafolha
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El senador Flávio Bolsonaro y el mandatario Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva definirán la presidencia de Brasil en una segunda vuelta prevista para el 25 de octubre, según las previsiones de Datafolha del domingo.
items.body:
El senador Flávio Bolsonaro y el mandatario Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva definirán la presidencia de Brasil en una segunda vuelta prevista para el 25 de octubre, según las previsiones de Datafolha del domingo.
Según el recuento del Tribunal Superior Electoral (TSE), con el 64,81% de los votos escrutados, Bolsonaro lidera la carrera con un 49,58% de los sufragios, seguido de Lula con un 42,25%.
Para ganar en la primera vuelta, un candidato debe superar el 50% de los votos válidos.

items.title: CSL strikes rare disease drug deal worth up to $1.6 billion with Swiss firm Alentis
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Australia's CSL said on Monday it had entered into an agreement with Switzerland-based Alentis Therapeutics to co-develop and co-promote a treatment for rare kidney and liver diseases, in a deal worth up to $1.6 billion before development funding.
items.body:
Australia's CSL (CSL.AX) said on Monday it had entered into an agreement with Switzerland-based Alentis Therapeutics to co-develop and co-promote a treatment for rare kidney and liver diseases, in a deal worth up to $1.6 billion before development funding.
Under the partnership, CSL will make an upfront payment of $355 million, while Alentis is eligible for up to $1.2 billion in commercial milestone payments.
The deal gives the Australian biotech giant rights to jointly develop and commercialise lixudebart, a potential first-in-class treatment being studied for rare kidney and liver diseases.
Lixudebart, formerly known as ALE.F02, is currently in a Phase 2 trial for a rare autoimmune kidney disease that can cause irreversible kidney damage and end-stage renal disease.
The drug was granted orphan drug designation — a special status granted by the US FDA to investigational therapies intended to prevent, diagnose, or treat rare diseases or conditions — for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or chronic lung disease, in 2024.
The companies also plan to advance the drug as a potential treatment for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a chronic kidney disease, and primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), a chronic liver disease for which there is currently no approved therapy.
Once commercialised, global profits from the drug will be shared 55% to CSL and 45% to Alentis.

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Brent crude futures climbed to $103.06 a barrel.
items.body:
Oil prices rose on Monday after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said they [USN:S8N441065 TEXT:"launched"] ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area, raising concerns about production at the top exporter in the region.
Brent crude futures climbed 81 cents, or 0.79%, to $103.06 a barrel by 2202 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $91.57 a barrel, up 46 cents, or 0.50%.

items.title: トランプ氏、民主党勝利なら支援消極姿勢　オハイオ州で演説
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Bo Erickson　Nandita Bose

[バンダリア（米オハイオ州） ３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Bo Erickson　Nandita Bose

[バンダリア（米オハイオ州） ３日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は３日、中間選挙に向けオハイオ州で集会を開いた。民主党を下品な言葉で攻撃する一方、共和党が選挙で勝利すれば財政支援を提供すると約束した。民主党が勝利した場合は、州への協力に消極的になると警告した。

トランプ氏は、ジョン・ハステッド上院議員やオハイオ州知事選候補のビベック・ラマスワミ氏ら共和党候補を応援する集会で「とにかく投票に行ってほしい」と訴えた。「そうすればわれわれは勝つ。大勝して、やつらに思い知らせてやる」と述べた。

１１月３日の選挙では、全米各地の共和党現職上院議員が厳しい政治的逆風に直面している。米国とイスラエルによる対イラン戦争でガソリンや生活必需品の価格が高止まりする中、トランプ氏の支持率はここ数カ月低下している。ハステッド氏とラマスワミ氏はいずれも民主党候補と接戦を繰り広げている。

世論調査では、僅差で勢力が分かれる上下両院の支配権を決める中間選挙で民主党が議席を伸ばす可能性が示されている。しかしトランプ氏は、共和党が批判派の予想を上回る結果を出すと主張。オハイオ州の集会で、「大きなサプライズがあると思う。彼らは何が起きているか分かっていない」と語った。

オハイオ州の上院選は、接戦と評価される全米８つの選挙区の一つ。

トランプ氏は演説で、民主党を繰り返し攻撃し、「ばかなろくでなしども」と呼ぶ場面もあった。一方、共和党が権力を維持すれば、オハイオ州の当局者は政権と直接のパイプを持ち、連邦政府の支援を確保しやすくなると訴えた。

オハイオ州で選出された共和党当局者が州への資金を求めて頻繁に電話をかけてくると述べ、民主党候補が主要選挙で勝利した場合には要求に応じる気になれないとした。

items.title: Canada boss Marsch calls for severe punishment for Man City
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Canada coach Jesse Marsch has called for Manchester City to be punished severely over breaches of Premier League financial rules, saying his experience managing against the club left him convinced there were inconsistencies in the way it operated.
items.body:
Canada coach Jesse Marsch has called for Manchester City to be punished severely over breaches of Premier League financial rules, saying his experience managing against the club left him convinced there were inconsistencies in the way it operated.
City were found guilty of [USN:L6N45L10S TEXT:"serious breaches"] of Premier League financial rules over nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, with the league alleging the club used "sham" commercial contracts to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19 billion).
The club has denied wrongdoing, saying the verdict contained material errors of law, principle and fact, and [USN:L1N45O0BQ TEXT:"filed an appeal"] on Thursday against the independent commission ruling.
Marsch, who managed Leeds United from 2022 to 2023, said the disparity between the clubs had been apparent to him during his time in England.
"I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew," Marsch told the Guardian in an interview published on Sunday.
Marsch also pointed to the 2022 summer transfer window, when Leeds sold Raphinha to Barcelona and Kalvin Phillips to City, while both clubs reported making money.
"That summer (2022), us and Man City were the only teams that said we made money. For us, we did make money, because we sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips. We had a lot left over from what we bought," he said.
"At the time, we weren't in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn't have deep pockets. Whereas when Man City says this, I was literally like, 'Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?'"
The American coach was also sceptical about City's signing of Erling Haaland from Borussia Dortmund that summer.
"When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it's like: 'Yeah, OK, sure!' So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, 'This is football'," Marsch said.
Reuters has contacted Manchester City for comment on Marsch's remarks.
City's appeal will be heard privately by an independent three-member board.
Potential sanctions include fines, points deductions and other sporting penalties, with relegation or the removal of titles also discussed as possible outcomes. It remains unclear whether any sanctions would be imposed before the appeal is decided.
($1 = 0.7554 pounds)

"When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it's like: 'Yeah, OK, sure!' So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, 'This is football'," Marsch said.
Reuters has contacted Manchester City for comment on Marsch's remarks.
City's appeal will be heard privately by an independent three-member board.
Potential sanctions include fines, points deductions and other sporting penalties, with relegation or the removal of titles also discussed as possible outcomes. It remains unclear whether any sanctions would be imposed before the appeal is decided.
($1 = 0.7554 pounds)

items.title: 独首相、ウクライナに追加軍事支援10億ユーロ　ロシアの脅しに屈せずと強調
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andreas Rinke　Felix Hoske

［キーウ　４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Andreas Rinke　Felix Hoske

［キーウ　４日　ロイター］ - ドイツのメルツ首相は４日、ウクライナ首都キーウを訪問し、ロシアによる脅しに屈してウクライナへの支援を撤回することはないと表明し、１０億ユーロ（１１億ドル）の追加軍事支援を実施すると発表した。

メルツ氏はウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領とともに、４年間にわたる戦争で死亡した兵士の追悼施設や、先週のドローン（無人機）攻撃で少なくとも２人が死亡した科学アカデミーを訪れた。キーウでは滞在中、空襲警報が繰り返し鳴り、爆発音も聞かれた。

ロシアはここ数週間、キーウなどの都市へのドローン攻撃を激化させ、通信や電力、交通インフラのほか、軍事施設を標的にしている。

メルツ氏はゼレンスキー氏との共同記者会見で、ロシアがウクライナ国民の士気をくじこうとしていると指摘。エネルギー部門の復旧に３億５０００万ユーロを拠出すると発表し、ドイツは引き続きウクライナに対する最大の支援国だと強調した。

さらにメルツ氏は「われわれがこれを行うのはウクライナの領土保全を守るためだけではない。欧州の安全保障に関わる問題であり、われわれ自身の利益のためでもある」と述べた上で、ロシアによるサイバー攻撃や偽情報活動が欧州の民主主義秩序を脅かしているとして「（支援は）われわれが脅迫に屈しないことを示している」と語った。

複数のドイツ政府高官によると、メルツ氏に同行した企業幹部らは、ウクライナ政府や同国企業と計１４件、総額約６６億ユーロの契約を締結した。ウクライナはドイツ防衛企業ディール・ディフェンスと防空ミサイル「ＩＲＩＳ－Ｔ」の供給で合意したほか、ヘンゾルトとはレーダー装備、クアンタム・システムズとはジェット式ドローン迎撃機を巡る契約を結んだ。

ゼレンスキー氏は「今回の訪問で重要なのは、ドイツがウクライナを支援するだけでなく、ウクライナも知識や経験、受注を共有していることだ。これはドイツの雇用につながる」とその意義に言及。クアンタム・システムズが開発した「ＳＰＹＳ」と呼ばれる新型ジェット式ドローン迎撃機について、有望な成果を示していると評価した。またウクライナとドイツは幅広い防衛協定の締結に近づいていると明らかにした。

ロシアがこの夏以降、民間・軍事インフラを狙って連日数十機を投入している高速のジェット式攻撃ドローン数は、従来のプロペラ式に比べて速度が大幅に速く、ウクライナ側は迎撃に苦戦している。

キーウのクリチコ市長の話では、４日のロシア側の攻撃の１つはドニプロ川に架かるノーザン橋に命中し、路面が損傷するとともに爆発で２人が負傷し、周辺の温水供給設備も被害を受けた。

ゼレンスキー氏は、ロシアがインフラへの空爆を激化させているのは、戦場で後退を余儀なくされているためだと主張し、ウクライナ側も報復すると表明した。ロシアのプーチン大統領がウクライナの主要都市から住民を退避させようとしているとの見方を示した。

一方ゼレンスキー氏は、米国のウィットコフ和平担当特使から、３者協議をできるだけ早く再開するよう求めるメッセージを受け取ったとも発言。ウクライナは今月中の協議に応じる用意があり、ロシアの参加を期待していると説明しつつも、戦争を終結させるには西側諸国がロシア政府への圧力を一段と強める必要があると訴えた。

items.title: ロシアがジェット推進式ドローン技術を北朝鮮と共有の可能性＝ゼレンスキー氏
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [キーウ ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[キーウ ４日 ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は４日、ロシアが長年の同盟国である北朝鮮にジェット推進式ドローンの技術を共有した可能性があるとの見解を示した。

ここ数週間、ロシアはウクライナに対するジェット推進式ドローンの使用を大幅に増やしており、ウクライナ側には現時点で戦闘機を使用する以外に、これに対抗する有効な手段がない。

対ウクライナ戦争で北朝鮮はロシアに数百万発の砲弾や弾道ミサイルを提供している。

ロシアが最新世代のジェット推進式ドローンの技術を北朝鮮と共有したかどうか尋ねられたゼレンスキー氏は、記者団に対し「もちろんだ」と答えた。

その上で「ロシアは北朝鮮と全ての技術を共有している。弾道ミサイルなどについては分からないが、北朝鮮がロシアにミサイルを提供していたことを考えると、そうだろう」と語った。

これとは別に、ゼレンスキー氏が９月の国連総会で、ロシア側で戦っていた際に捕虜となった北朝鮮兵２人を韓国に移送したと公表したことに韓国が反発し、謝罪を求めていることについて、「韓国はわれわれに北朝鮮兵士を引き渡すよう求めてきた。韓国の憲法によれば、兵士らは韓国国民なのでわれわれは２人を引き渡した」と述べた。

韓国の李在明大統領は２日、ウクライナが北朝鮮兵２人の移送について秘密保持で合意していたことを認め、謝罪しなければ、追加措置を取ると警告したが、ゼレンスキー氏は李氏の発言には言及しなかった。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [サンパウロ ３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[サンパウロ ３日 ロイター] - ブラジルで４日に実施された大統領選の第１回投票は、右派のフラビオ・ボルソナロ上院議員が左派のルラ大統領をリードしている。

選挙管理当局である選挙裁判所が公表した開票序盤の集計によると、開票率１０．０８％の時点で、白票と無効票を除く有効投票の得票率は、ボルソナロ氏が５０．９６％、ルラ氏が４０．７８％となっている。

有効投票の過半数を獲得する候補がいなければ、上位２人が１０月２５日の決選投票に進む。

ボルソナロ氏への支持が強い南部の州は開票結果の報告が早いことが多く、ルラ氏の地盤である北東部の票は通常、集計が後になる。

items.title: A roadmap for Andy Burnham to reverse Brexit
items.author: Hugo Dixon
items.creator: Hugo Dixon
items.summary: Britain’s prime minister says the country could rejoin the European Union. To do so, he will first have to decide if he wants to take that step, then win an election, and then persuade the 27-country bloc to readmit its former member. Here is how he could go about it.
items.body:
Andy Burnham [USN:L8N45L233 TEXT:"said"] last week that the United Kingdom could “go all the way” and rejoin the European Union. How could Britain’s new prime minister complete such a journey given the trauma Britain has suffered following the 2016 Brexit referendum and the trouble it inflicted on its European partners in the process?
Burnham will have to start by deciding that he definitely wants to rejoin the EU. He will then have to win a general election based on that premise and then persuade the 27-country bloc to readmit its former member. Here is a roadmap.
Burnham said in his speech to his Labour Party’s conference that “Brexit has done more harm than good”. Britain’s economic output is 6-8% lower than it would have been if it had stayed in the EU, according to a recent paper published by the National Bureau of Economic Research. Brexit has also damaged both the UK’s and the EU’s power, weakening the continent at a time of geopolitical turmoil.
The prime minister laid out a series of options, only one of which was to rejoin the EU. The alternatives are to join Europe’s customs union or single market, negotiate a bespoke deal with the bloc like the one Canada is discussing, or leave things as they are. There are good reasons for going the whole way.
Becoming a member of the EU’s customs union would simplify trade in goods across the English Channel. But it would not boost trade in services, which accounts for about 80% of UK output. It would also require Britain to align its trade policy with the EU’s but not have any vote on it.
Joining the single market would smooth trade in services as well as goods. However, Britain would have to accept free movement of people across the EU and follow all the bloc’s economic regulations, again without a say in how they are formed.
Canada and the EU are discussing joining forces to help them both resist intimidation by China, the United States and Russia. The [USN:L6N45A0WZ TEXT:"idea"] is to boost resilience in everything from energy and rare earths to technology and defence equipment. While the UK also needs to stand up to bullies, it is more closely entwined with the EU than Canada. So although a “resilience pact” could be a good step to rejoining, full membership with a seat at the decision-making table remains the best destination.
CONVINCING VOTERS Burnham says a decision on rejoining the EU would have to wait until after a general election, which must be held no later than 2029. His Labour Party is favourite to win the most seats, probably without an overall majority, according to Oddschecker. But it is vying with Reform UK, the anti-EU party led by Nigel Farage, for first place.
One reason for going all the way is that this is more popular than joining either the single market or the customs union, according to polling by YouGov for Best for Britain, the pro-EU group. Their research also shows that Labour will perform better at the next election if it backs full EU membership.
Burnham would still have to win the election, though. Key to this would be to convince voters that rejoining the EU would help address their main concerns: migration, the economy, security, and health. This is where the prime minister’s charisma should be an asset.
If Labour won a general election, perhaps forming a coalition with the pro-European Liberal Democrats, that would not be the end of the story. Burnham says there might also be a referendum on reversing Brexit.
One way to make it easier to win such a plebiscite would be to offer voters a simple question about the principle of rejoining the EU, while leaving the details to parliament. This would be a mirror image of the Brexit referendum, which consulted voters before the government had negotiated an exit deal. Such a vote could take place immediately after an election.
CONVINCING THE EU Even then, however, Britain could not re-enter the bloc by expressing its desire to do so. It would have to persuade the EU’s 27 existing members to let it back into the club.
The UK would not get the same terms it enjoyed before, when it received a £4.5 billion rebate on its annual membership fee. It might also have to sign up to eventually join the euro, though this would not necessarily be a dealbreaker. EU members such as Poland and Sweden still have their currencies.
Britain has much to contribute to the EU. Its capable military and its $4.3 trillion economy, Europe’s second largest after Germany’s, are key assets.
A trickier challenge will be persuading the EU that Britain is coming back for good. Even if Burnham charms the bloc’s leaders, starting with a summit planned for November, they will worry that a future anti-EU government in Westminster will pull the UK out for a second time.
While the prime minister cannot give a cast-iron guarantee that this will not happen, he can mitigate the risk. His plan to [USN:S8N44301D TEXT:"change"] Britain's voting system if he wins the next election would, if successful, make it impossible for an anti-EU party to obtain a parliamentary majority with as little as 30% of the vote, as is theoretically the case today. Under a more proportional voting system, a future anti-EU government would need the support of nearer half the electorate to push through its agenda.
What is more, if Burnham called a referendum to take Britain back into the EU, he could set the threshold of consent at, say, 55% or 60%. This would help establish the precedent that a similar super majority would be needed for any subsequent attempt to take the UK out.
The EU is weak and divided. Whether it rises to the [USN:L6N3XB0W3 TEXT:"challenges"] presented by Russia, China and the United States and tackles its own economic woes will help determine whether the UK wants to rejoin. If far-right parties take power in France and Germany, the EU will be a less attractive club. By contrast, if the bloc boosts its defences, helps Ukraine stave off Russia’s invasion and enacts long-promised reforms to boost its productivity, Burnham – and many Britons – will be clamouring to rejoin.

items.title: Lula não jogou bandeira do Brasil no chão após votar, mas a entregou a fotógrafo
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) não atirou no chão uma bandeira do Brasil após votar neste domingo, como alegam posts nas redes sociais que reproduzem um vídeo omitindo o momento em que Lula entrega o item ao seu fotógrafo, Ricardo Stuckert.
items.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) não atirou no chão uma bandeira do Brasil após votar neste domingo, como alegam posts nas redes sociais que reproduzem um vídeo omitindo o momento em que Lula entrega o item ao seu fotógrafo, Ricardo Stuckert .
Estes são os principais detalhes:
“Revoltante! Lula amassa bandeira do Brasil e joga no chão”, dizem publicações no Facebook, no Instagram e no Threads com as imagens.
O presidente votou em São Bernardo do Campo (SP) e posou para fotos ao lado do vice-presidente e candidato à reeleição, Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), segurando a bandeira nacional.
Logo em seguida, Lula caminha para deixar o local de votação e entrega rapidamente a bandeira a Stuckert, mas o enquadramento do vídeo usado nos posts checados não permite ver a passagem do objeto para o fotógrafo.
O momento em que Lula entregou a bandeira a Stuckert apareceu na transmissão ao vivo da GloboNews .
Veredicto: Falso. Lula entregou ao seu fotógrafo a bandeira do Brasil após votar, e não a jogou no chão.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: Improving special teams high on Bruins' agenda as Senators visit
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Another first is on tap for the Boston Bruins.
items.body:
Another first is on tap for the Boston Bruins.
After splitting a back-to-back road trip, Boston opens a three-game homestand with its first Atlantic Division test of the season against the Ottawa Senators on Monday night.
The Bruins could not pull off a sweep of two teams playing their home openers, taking a 4-1 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Saturday after beating the Winnipeg Jets 4-3 on JJ Peterka's game-winner in overtime a night earlier.
"Special teams were probably the difference, both ways. But I really liked our 5-on-5 game," Boston coach Marco Sturm said in Minnesota. "We didn't really give them much. Our first period was outstanding. A lot of good things happened (on Saturday). ... Guys battled hard. They really did."
Both of Boston's specialty units have struggled, with the power play yet to score in six chances and the penalty kill going 4-for-7. On Saturday, Tanner Jeannot gave the Bruins a 1-0 lead in just 1:53, but Minnesota took control with a pair of power-play goals in the second period.
Fellow fourth-liner Mark Kastelic set up Jeannot's goal with a touch feed through his legs, giving him a team-high three points (one goal, two assists).
"He's been playing unreal. I told him before the game, 'Just keep doing what you're doing,'" Jeannot said. "He's the heartbeat of this team. He's doing everything -- he's putting his body on the line, he's getting points right now. It's been a lot of fun playing with him."
Peterka scored in Boston's first two games. He recorded his third straight 25-goal season last year with the Utah Mammoth, who play in Boston on Thursday.
The Bruins figure to turn back to Jeremy Swayman in goal after reigning AHL Most Valuable Player Michael DiPietro made his Boston debut with a 26-save effort. It was the 27-year-old's first NHL start since 2022, when he was a member of the Vancouver Canucks.
"You definitely learn from your mistakes. Like I said, obviously not the outcome that I wanted, and I own that," DiPietro said. "I just have to be better and continue to work and try my best."
Ottawa's wait for its season opener -- the longest of any NHL team -- was worth it after a 3-2 win over the host Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday.
However, top defenseman Jake Sanderson played only 4:29 before exiting with a nagging lower-body injury, and there was no update on his status following the game. The Senators were already starting the season without defenseman Artem Zub (knee).
"We'll know more in the next few days, but Sandy was smart enough to pull himself early enough that he didn't reaggravate it too badly," Ottawa coach Travis Green said. "He just felt that it was coming and took himself out."
Sanderson, who left a preseason game a week earlier with a different injury, smashed his stick in frustration upon returning to the bench.
"He's going to put everything he can into it and he'll be back in no time," new Senators captain Thomas Chabot said of Sanderson.
Following Sanderson's exit, the Senators had to rally from a 2-1 deficit, outshooting their archrivals 16-5 in the final frame and getting the game-winning goal from Stephen Halliday with 10:14 remaining.
Chabot had a goal and an assist while playing 27:06, Michael Amadio also scored and Claude Giroux dished out a pair of helpers. Former Bruin Linus Ullmark, who went on a 14-4-3 run late last season, made 27 saves to lift Ottawa to its third straight season-opening win under Green.
"I thought the third period was our best," Chabot said. "We played exactly the way that we wanted to play. I'm just glad we got it done."
--Field Level Media

items.body:
Com 41,57% das seções eleitorais apuradas nas eleições presidenciais deste domingo, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderava com 50,41% dos votos válidos, seguido pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) com 41,44%, de acordo com dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).
Alguns Estados onde Flávio está liderando estão com a apuração mais adiantada do que em unidades da Federação onde Lula aparece na frente.
Para vencer a eleição já neste domingo, um candidato precisa conquistar mais de 50% dos votos válidos.

items.title: Britain set to levy tariffs on Chinese electric cars, The Times reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Britain is considering imposing tariffs on Chinese electric vehicle imports amid concerns that Beijing is flooding the market with state-subsidised cars, the Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
items.body:
Britain is considering imposing tariffs on Chinese electric vehicle imports amid concerns that Beijing is flooding the market with state-subsidised cars, the Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
Business minister Jonathan Reynolds is drawing up a package of potential tariffs on Chinese vehicle imports, the report said, citing concerns that Chinese manufacturers are "dumping" subsidised vehicles into Britain.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Asked to comment, a spokesperson from the British government told Reuters no tariffs have been imposed on Chinese EVs.
"We continue to engage closely with industry so that our approach reflects the sector’s and UK’s national interests," the spokesperson said in an email.
British ministers are ready to match the European Union's 45% levy on Chinese electric cars, the Times said, to avoid the pain of "Made in Europe" proposals, which could impact UK companies selling into the EU.
The EU's "[USN:L8N42K09E TEXT:"Made in Europe"]" policy is aimed at reducing reliance on Chinese components by prioritising European-made goods, raising concerns among British automakers that supply parts into European manufacturing chains and sell vehicles across the bloc.
Burnham [USN:L8N45E0EA TEXT:"said"] last month he would make the case that Britain should be treated as a "trusted partner" under the proposed EU rules, warning that excluding the UK could damage its car industry.
The Financial Times reported in September [USN:FWN45G1EO TEXT:"that Brussels had urged"] British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to align more closely with EU trade policy and raise tariffs on Chinese cars if Britain wants to avoid the "made in Europe" barriers.
According to the Times, citing senior government sources, ministers believe any decision on tariffs should be based on Britain's national interest rather than automatically following the EU's lead.

items.title: FIA to investigate software bug after Bahrain GP in Malaysia
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Formula One's governing body has promised a full investigation into a software bug that caused chaos and forced the start of Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to be aborted with drivers feeling like they were in battery-powered cars made of Lego.
items.body:
Formula One's governing body has promised a full investigation into a software bug that caused chaos and forced the start of Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to be aborted with drivers feeling like they were in battery-powered cars made of Lego.
Ferrari's seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's four-time champion and[USN:L1N45Q023 TEXT:" eventual race winner Max Verstappen "]were among several affected by the glitch on a formation lap after torrential rain and [USN:L1N45Q01D TEXT:"a long delay "]at Malaysia's steamy Sepang circuit.
Verstappen compared the experience to a[USN:L6N43703Y TEXT:" 'Lego race"]' held at Silverstone before the British Grand Prix while Hamilton, the sport's most successful driver of all time, had to stop his car on track and re-start it in what he said was a career first.
The episode was the latest in a difficult first season for the new era of cars and engines, with drivers at the pinnacle of motorsport unhappy since the opening race with the power units' increased electrical component and the need for energy management.
The governing FIA said afterwards that "an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars."
"As a result, the FIA technical department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain, enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race.
“This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue."
The FIA's single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis told reporters the lack of pre-season testing in wet conditions had played a part in the chaos.
"Some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely," he said. “That bug prevented the power from being redeployed, and for the cars to start again.
"I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time, and not have such a situation."
Sepang was the first race weekend of the season with wet conditions, although the track dried during the race.
"Sometimes things fall through the net and people learn, and you do a better job next time,” said Tombazis.

“This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue."
The FIA's single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis told reporters the lack of pre-season testing in wet conditions had played a part in the chaos.

items.body:
Com 31,9% das seções eleitorais apuradas nas eleições presidenciais deste domingo, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderava com 50,74% dos votos válidos, seguido pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), com 41,14%, de acordo com dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).
Alguns Estados onde Flávio está liderando estão com a apuração mais avançada do que em unidades da Federação onde Lula aparece na frente.
Para vencer a eleição em primeiro turno já neste domingo, um candidato precisa conquistar mais de 50% dos votos válidos.

items.title: US removes B-1 bombers from UK base amid security concerns
items.author: Svea Herbst-Bayliss
items.creator: Svea Herbst-Bayliss
items.summary: The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one week after several men were arrested there on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday.
items.body:
The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one week after several men were arrested there on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday.
A dozen B-1 bombers were stationed at RAF Fairford air base, located northwest of London. The planes had been used for US strikes on Iran.
"While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States," a Pentagon spokesman wrote in an email.
Britain has "strong indications" that [USN:L1N45M0MW TEXT:"Iran was involved"] in a [USN:L1N45O076 TEXT:"suspected plot"] targeting the base, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday. Iran said accusations linking Tehran to the alleged plan were baseless and summoned the British ambassador in Tehran over the issue.
The Wall Street Journal first reported that the aircraft were removed from the base amid security concerns over suspected terror plots against the facility.
The British government had allowed the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
US President [USN:L8N45K0CX TEXT:"Donald Trump said those involved in the plot"] had planned "big damage" while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also pointed to the "hands of a foreign actor."

items.title: Portugal secure place in Nations League quarter-finals
items.author: Mark Gleeson
items.creator: Mark Gleeson
items.summary: Title holders Portugal maintained their 100% record in the Nations League with a 2-1 home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in the March quarter-finals and shift the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from the squad last week.
items.body:
Title holders Portugal maintained their 100% record in the Nations League with a 2-1 home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in the March quarter-finals and shift the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from the squad last week.
Goncalo Ramos netted 11 minutes from time to ensure Portugal secured a top-two finish in Group A4 as they moved six points ahead of second-placed Denmark, who won 1-0 at Wales.
The Netherlands took over at the top of Group A2, after beating Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven, but only on goal difference from Greece, who held on grimly for a goalless draw at home to Germany in Thessaloniki.
Portugal were still under a cloud from Ronaldo’s dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, although they were triumphant without him in Denmark last Thursday after he walked out on the squad, and continued their winning ways in Porto on Sunday.
Norway took the lead in the 36th minute from centre-back Kristoffer Ajer, who hit a dipping half-volley from the edge of the box. But if that effort was sumptuous, Joao Cancelo’s thrashing effort to equalise two minutes later was even more awe-inspiring.
Ramos’ winner came off his calf after Joao Felix had headed across goal for him to score.
“You need a lot of technical quality to beat Norway," said the Portugal coach.
"We won without putting in a performance like the one against Denmark, but the important thing was the victory and qualification. I had a lot of belief in this team, but perhaps I didn’t expect us to have four wins from our first four games,” Jorge Jesus added.
RED CARD SOURS PORTUGAL'S WIN Portugal’s win was soured by a red card for Francisco Conceicao four minutes from time. He gave the referee a cynical thumbs up after receiving a yellow card and was immediately handed his marching orders.
Wales goalkeeper Danny Ward made several key saves to keep Denmark at bay in Cardiff, but then conceded a penalty with a foul on Gustav Isaksen, allowing Rasmus Hojlund to tuck away a 75th-minute penalty to win their tie.
The Netherlands, with captain Virgil van Dijk celebrating a 100th cap, went ahead against Serbia when Teun Koopmeiners’s 31st-minute freekick evaded all in the penalty area and crept into the corner.
But the visitors were level within four minutes as Aleksa Terzic crossed for teenager Mihajlo Cvetkovic to rise over Koopmeiners and head in his first international goal.
ZIRKZEE GRABS DUTCH WINNER It took until the 72nd minute to go back ahead when Denzel Dumfries’ low cross was turned back across the goal by Tijjani Reijnders, sliding in at the far post, and tapped in by Joshua Zirkzee, who received a late call-up to the Dutch squad last week.
Germany dominated away against Greece, but Jurgen Klopp’s inexperienced side could not find the net, and they have won only one of their first four games under the new coach.
Austria needed a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Kosovo but still have a three-point lead at the top of Group B3 after the Republic of Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 behind closed doors in the Serbian town of Backa Topola.
In Group D2, Abdulakh Khaybulayev’s first-half goal was enough to send Azerbaijan top of the standings with a 1-0 win over previously unbeaten Lithuania, while veteran Teddy Teuma came on as a second-half substitute to hand Malta a 1-0 home win over Andorra in Group D1.

Oct 4 : Title holders Portugal maintained their 100 per cent record in the Nations League with a 2-1 home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in the March quarter-finals and shift the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from the squad last week.
Goncalo Ramos netted 11 minutes from time to ensure Portugal secured a top-two finish in Group A4 as they moved six points ahead of second-placed Denmark, who won 1-0 at Wales.
The Netherlands took over at the top of Group A2, after beating Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven, but only on goal difference from Greece, who held on grimly for a goalless draw at home to Germany in Thessaloniki.
Portugal were still under a cloud from Ronaldo’s dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, although they were triumphant without him in Denmark last Thursday after he walked out on the squad, and continued their winning ways in Porto on Sunday.

Norway took the lead in the 36th minute from centre-back Kristoffer Ajer, who hit a dipping half-volley from the edge of the box. But if that effort was sumptuous, Joao Cancelo’s thrashing effort to equalise two minutes later was even more awe-inspiring.
Ramos’ winner came off his calf after Joao Felix had headed across goal for him to score.
“You need a lot of technical quality to beat Norway," said the Portugal coach.
"We won without putting in a performance like the one against Denmark, but the important thing was the victory and qualification. I had a lot of belief in this team, but perhaps I didn’t expect us to have four wins from our first four games,” Jorge Jesus added.
RED CARD SOURS PORTUGAL'S WIN
Portugal’s win was soured by a red card for Francisco Conceicao four minutes from time. He gave the referee a cynical thumbs up after receiving a yellow card and was immediately handed his marching orders.
Wales goalkeeper Danny Ward made several key saves to keep Denmark at bay in Cardiff, but then conceded a penalty with a foul on Gustav Isaksen, allowing Rasmus Hojlund to tuck away a 75th-minute penalty to win their tie. 
The Netherlands, with captain Virgil van Dijk celebrating a 100th cap, went ahead against Serbia when Teun Koopmeiners’s 31st-minute freekick evaded all in the penalty area and crept into the corner.
But the visitors were level within four minutes as Aleksa Terzic crossed for teenager Mihajlo Cvetkovic to rise over Koopmeiners and head in his first international goal.
ZIRKZEE GRABS DUTCH WINNER
It took until the 72nd minute to go back ahead when Denzel Dumfries’ low cross was turned back across the goal by Tijjani Reijnders, sliding in at the far post, and tapped in by Joshua Zirkzee, who received a late call-up to the Dutch squad last week. 
Germany dominated away against Greece, but Jurgen Klopp’s inexperienced side could not find the net, and they have won only one of their first four games under the new coach.
Austria needed a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Kosovo but still have a three-point lead at the top of Group B3 after the Republic of Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 behind closed doors in the Serbian town of Backa Topola.
In Group D2, Abdulakh Khaybulayev’s first-half goal was enough to send Azerbaijan top of the standings with a 1-0 win over previously unbeaten Lithuania, while veteran Teddy Teuma came on as a second-half substitute to hand Malta a 1-0 home win over Andorra in Group D1. 
(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; editing by Pritha Sarkar)

items.title: Posts inventam resultados de votações no exterior ainda em andamento
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Posts nas redes sociais sobre as eleições deste domingo inventam resultados de votações no exterior ainda em andamento, como nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá, e os misturam com supostos números impressos nos boletins de urna de países onde o pleito já se encerrou.
items.body:
Posts nas redes sociais sobre as eleições deste domingo inventam resultados de votações no exterior ainda em andamento, como nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá, e os misturam com supostos números impressos nos boletins de urna de países onde o pleito já se encerrou.
O conteúdo tem o título “votação no exterior” e diz mostrar os resultados atualizados “conforme boletins divulgados” pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), reproduzindo uma lista de 42 países e as supostas votações dos candidatos Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em cada um.
A montagem, que circula no Facebook e no Instagram, afirma que Lula obteve 23.992 votos no exterior, enquanto Flávio somou 71.601.
Há 918.876 eleitores aptos a votar em 186 cidades no exterior, segundo o TSE, exclusivamente para o cargo de presidente. Em todos os países, a votação ocorre das 8h às 17h, de acordo com o fuso horário local .
Por isso, a votação teve início às 16h deste sábado em Wellington, capital da Nova Zelândia, e terminará às 21h deste domingo em San Francisco e Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos, e em Vancouver, no Canadá, segundo levantamento do Poder360 .
Eleitores de parte dos países mencionados seguiam votando quando os posts começaram a ser compartilhados, na manhã deste domingo, como de Estados Unidos, Canadá, México, Argentina e Chile. Portanto, seria impossível saber o resultado do pleito nesses locais.
Nos países da Oceania e da Ásia , a votação já havia encerrado. A apuração oficial só começou a ser divulgada pelo TSE depois das 17h, no horário de Brasília, mas os boletins de urna impressos após o fim da votação permitiram o acesso a alguns desses resultados ao longo deste domingo.
Até as 17h45min, com 59,96% das seções no exterior apuradas pelo TSE , Lula tinha 112.644 votos (52,57%) em países estrangeiros, à frente de Flávio, com 81.069 votos (37,83%).
VEREDICTO Falso. Os posts divulgam resultados de votações no exterior antes do fechamento das urnas em uma série de países mencionados.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro aventaja a Lula en primera vuelta de elecciones Brasil: primeros recuentos
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro aventajaba al presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil el domingo, según un recuento preliminar del tribunal electoral del país.
items.body:
El senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro aventajaba al presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil el domingo, según un recuento preliminar del tribunal electoral del país.
Con el 10,08% de los votos escrutados, Bolsonaro obtenía el 50,96% de los votos válidos, excluyendo los sufragios en blanco y nulos, frente al 40,78% de Lula, según el tribunal.
Si ningún candidato obtiene más del 50% de los votos válidos, los dos aspirantes más votados pasarán a una segunda vuelta el 25 de octubre.
Los estados del sur, inclinados hacia Bolsonaro, suelen ser los primeros en reportar resultados, mientras que los votos del bastión de Lula en el noreste generalmente se contabilizan más tarde.
