items.title: Colorado State DC out after mid-game demotion
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The in-game decision by Colorado State head coach Jim Mora on Saturday to change defensive play-callers led to the dismissal of the Rams' defensive coordinator.
items.body:
The in-game decision by Colorado State head coach Jim Mora on Saturday to change defensive play-callers led to the dismissal of the Rams' defensive coordinator.
As he watched Oregon State pile up the yards in an eventual 56-26 loss, Mora told defensive coordinator Tyson Summers that he was done calling plays for the day. Mora transferred the duties to associate head coach and defensive line coach Kenny McClendon.
When Summers departed the field after his demotion, that ended his tenure at Colorado State.
"Tyson was relieved of his play-calling duties. He left the field, and he is no longer with this football program," Mora said postgame. "That is permanent."
The change occurred in the first half, per local reports. At halftime, the Beavers had a 35-14 lead. Oregon State finished with 650 yards of total offense -- 223 on the ground and 427 via air as Beavers quarterback Braden Atkinson finished the game 31-of-34 passing with five touchdowns.
Summers, 46, has an extensive coaching background, beginning in the college ranks at his alma mater - Presbyterian - in 2003. He got his first chance as a defensive coordinator at UCF (2012-14), followed by a season as DC and safeties coach at Colorado State, departing for a two-year stint as head coach at Georgia Southern.
Summers also spent two seasons as the DC at Colorado (2019-20), then three at Western Kentucky in the same role (2022-24) before returning to Colorado State in 2025 as DC under Jay Norvell.
When Norvell was fired seven games into last season, Summers took over as interim coach, and the Rams finished with an 0-5 record.
Colorado State (2-3), which has not finished above .500 since 2017, snatched Mora last fall from UConn, where he rebuilt the struggling program in four seasons. Previously the head coach at UCLA and in the NFL with the Atlanta Falcons and Seattle Seahawks, Mora kept Summers on board.
Mora, 64, said McClendon will be the defensive coordinator for the rest of the season.
"He was put in a very difficult situation, and he responded well, the players responded well," Mora said. "Very first play he called as a defensive coordinator in his entire life was a sack, caused a fumble. So we're going to get better, we're going to get a lot better. He's a good football coach."
Colorado State defeated Wyoming and Southern Utah to start the season, allowing 37 total points. Since then, in losses to BYU, UTSA and Oregon State, the Rams have surrendered 156 points -- an average of 52 per game.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Nunes Marques diz esperar judicialização das eleições, mas afirma que pleito transcorre normalmente
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou neste domingo ser esperado que candidatos acionem a Justiça com questionamentos relacionados às eleições, mas ponderou que a votação está transcorrendo com normalidade e transparência, também sem indícios de interferência internacional.
items.body:
O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou neste domingo ser esperado que candidatos acionem a Justiça com questionamentos relacionados às eleições, mas ponderou que a votação está transcorrendo com normalidade e transparência, também sem indícios de interferência internacional.
Em entrevista coletiva por volta das 14h com dados preliminares sobre a eleição, Nunes Marques afirmou que as urnas estão funcionando normalmente e não houve necessidade de uso de votação manual em nenhum ponto do país.
“Há uma tradição na justiça brasileira de judicialização, então seria de se esperar que os candidatos, não só à Presidência da República, mas deputados estaduais e federais e governadores batam às portas da Justiça com os seus questionamentos”, disse, citando como exemplos ações sobre abuso de poder político e econômico de candidatos.
“Estamos bastante confiantes de que até agora não temos ainda do que se queixar", disse Nunes Marques. "Tudo tem funcionado na maior normalidade e com a maior transparência possível.”
De acordo com o presidente do TSE, 1.121 urnas com algum tipo de falha foram substituídas, 0,2% do total.
Em relação a irregularidades, Nunes Marques afirmou que 59 pessoas foram conduzidas pela polícia por suspeita de crime eleitoral e mais de R$380 mil em espécie foram apreendidos.
Ele enfatizou que o TSE não identificou nenhum indicativo de interferência estrangeira nas eleições.
“Equipes que monitoram riscos internacionais não apontam qualquer tipo de risco”, afirmou.
O diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, afirmou mais cedo neste domingo que a corporação abriu [USN:L1N45Q03S TEXT:"investigação"] para apurar suposto esquema de financiamento de uma agenda de extrema-direita no Brasil pelo governo norte-americano de Donald Trump que teria entre os objetivos interferir nas eleições brasileiras. A investigação foi solicitada pela Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU).

items.title: Australia investiga los vínculos del copiloto de flydubai con el país, dice la policía
items.author: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
items.creator: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
items.summary: Una unidad antiterrorista australiana en la que participan varios organismos está investigando los vínculos con Australia del copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, quien apuñaló a su capitán y luego intentó secuestrar el avión, informó el domingo un portavoz de la policía.
items.body:
Una unidad antiterrorista australiana en la que participan varios organismos está investigando los vínculos con Australia del copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, quien apuñaló a su capitán y luego intentó secuestrar el avión, informó el domingo un portavoz de la policía.
El Equipo Conjunto Antiterrorista de Victoria, integrado por la policía federal, la policía estatal de Victoria y la agencia de inteligencia ASIO, estaba "investigando los vínculos de este hombre con Australia", dijo el portavoz de la Policía Federal Australiana.
Dos fuentes al tanto de la investigación indicaron que el copiloto estudió en una universidad de Melbourne, la capital del estado australiano de Victoria. Una tercera fuente señaló que estudió en la Universidad RMIT hace aproximadamente una década. La RMIT declinó hacer comentarios.
El copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, que el miércoles se dirigía a Israel desde Dubái, atacó al piloto con un hacha de emergencia, según dijo el sábado el fiscal general de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, que calificó el incidente de "ataque terrorista".
El vuelo FZ1073 debió de parecer una "montaña rusa vertical", ya que descendió 16.000 pies en unos 30 segundos antes de estabilizarse y aterrizar sin incidentes, según un instructor de aviación que recreó el descenso en un simulador de vuelo para Reuters.
COPILOTO DETENIDO EN LOS EAU Dos fuentes han afirmado que el copiloto es un ciudadano omaní llamado Hamam Al-Hamami. Las autoridades israelíes no han revelado el nombre del copiloto, pero han indicado que es de Omán. Las autoridades de los EAU y flydubai no han hecho pública la identidad del copiloto.
Reuters no ha podido contactar de forma independiente con Al-Hamami, que se encuentra bajo custodia en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, para recabar sus comentarios. Los Emiratos Árabes Unidos no han anunciado ningún cargo formal contra él y se desconoce si ha designado a un abogado. Omán no se ha pronunciado sobre el incidente.
Se evitó una catástrofe a bordo del vuelo FZ1073 después de que los pasajeros y la tripulación redujeran al copiloto, quien había atacado al capitán en lo que, según las autoridades israelíes, fue un intento de estrellar el avión, que transportaba a más de 170 pasajeros y tripulantes. El fiscal general de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos ha declarado que el copiloto había intentado tomar el control del avión.
La mayoría de los pasajeros a bordo eran ciudadanos israelíes.
Un piloto de reserva de flydubai que viajaba en ese vuelo tomó el control de la aeronave y la hizo aterrizar en el aeropuerto de Tabuk, en el noroeste de Arabia Saudita, donde el copiloto fue detenido por las autoridades sauditas y posteriormente trasladado a los Emiratos Árabes Unidos el jueves.
El Financial Times informó el domingo de que Al-Hamami habría visitado lo que describió como mezquitas radicales y páginas web extremistas durante su estancia en Australia, citando a dos personas familiarizadas con la investigación. Según el Financial Times, los servicios de inteligencia australianos tenían un expediente sobre esta persona.
Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato la información del FT. El Gobierno de Australia no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios fuera del horario laboral habitual.
El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, dijo que el copiloto había sido sometido a un adoctrinamiento islamista radical y que tenía claras intenciones suicidas, aunque no ha precisado cuándo ni dónde se produjo supuestamente dicho adoctrinamiento.
El domingo ordenó al Consejo de Seguridad Nacional que nombrara a un investigador para "llevar a cabo una revisión exhaustiva de todos los aspectos de seguridad relacionados con la aviación civil extranjera con destino a Israel".
Israel no mantiene relaciones diplomáticas oficiales con Omán, y Netanyahu también ha afirmado que no se permite a pilotos de esos países operar vuelos con destino a Israel. No está claro cómo llegó a ser asignado el copiloto al vuelo con destino a Tel Aviv.

items.title: Merz anuncia nuevas ayudas militares en Kiev y dice que Alemania no se dejará intimidar
items.author: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
items.creator: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
items.summary: Alemania no se dejará intimidar para que retire su apoyo a Ucrania, dijo el domingo el canciller Friedrich Merz, al anunciar una nueva ayuda militar de 1.000 millones de euros (1.100 millones de dólares) durante una visita a Kiev marcada por los ataques con drones rusos.
items.body:
Alemania no se dejará intimidar para que retire su apoyo a Ucrania, dijo el domingo el canciller Friedrich Merz, al anunciar una nueva ayuda militar de 1.000 millones de euros (1.100 millones de dólares) durante una visita a Kiev marcada por los ataques con drones rusos.
Las sirenas antiaéreas y las explosiones resonaron repetidamente en toda la capital ucraniana mientras Merz y el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, visitaban un monumento en memoria de los soldados fallecidos durante la guerra, que ya dura cuatro años, así como la Academia de Ciencias, donde al menos dos personas murieron en un ataque con drones la semana pasada.
Rusia ha intensificado sus ataques con drones contra Kiev y otras ciudades en las últimas semanas, apuntando a infraestructuras de telecomunicaciones, electricidad y transporte, así como contra instalaciones militares.
En una rueda de prensa junto a Zelenski, Merz dijo que Moscú estaba intentando minar la confianza del pueblo ucraniano y anunció una ayuda de 350 millones de euros para las reparaciones en el sector energético. Afirmó que Alemania seguía siendo el principal aliado de Ucrania.
"Hacemos esto no solo para proteger la integridad territorial de Ucrania; lo hacemos en nuestro propio interés, ya que es una cuestión de seguridad para Europa", dijo Merz, señalando que Rusia estaba llevando a cabo ciberataques y campañas de desinformación que atentaban contra el orden democrático europeo.
"Esto demuestra que no nos dejaremos intimidar", añadió.
Rusia ha afirmado que las acusaciones de guerra híbrida carecen de fundamento y son fruto de la histeria antirrusa.
Las autoridades indicaron que los directivos de las empresas alemanas, que viajaron con Merz, habían firmado 16 acuerdos con el Gobierno y empresas ucranianas por un valor aproximado de 6.500 millones de euros.
Entre esos acuerdos, Ucrania firmó un contrato con la firma alemana Diehl Defence para el suministro de misiles de defensa aérea IRIS-T, así como un acuerdo para equipos de radar con Hensoldt y para drones interceptores a reacción con Quantum Systems.
Zelenski elogió un nuevo dron interceptor a reacción, denominado SPYS y desarrollado por Quantum, por mostrar resultados prometedores. Dijo que Ucrania y Alemania estaban a punto de cerrar un amplio acuerdo de defensa que, según había declarado anteriormente, incluiría la producción de drones, misiles y software relacionado.
ZELENSKI SE COMPROMETE A RESPONDER Desde el verano boreal, Rusia ha atacado a diario infraestructuras civiles y militares con decenas de drones de ataque a reacción de alta velocidad, que Ucrania ha tenido dificultades para derribar debido a que son mucho más rápidos que las versiones anteriores con hélice.
Uno de los ataques rusos del domingo alcanzó el Puente del Norte, que cruza el río Dniéper, dañando su calzada, según informó el alcalde de Kiev, Vitali Klitschko, a través de Telegram. La explosión dejó dos heridos y dañó un sistema de suministro de agua caliente de la zona, añadió.
Zelenski dijo que la decisión de Rusia de intensificar los ataques aéreos contra objetivos de infraestructura se debía a los reveses que había sufrido en el campo de batalla, y prometió que Ucrania tomaría represalias. Aseguró que el presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, quería obligar a los residentes a huir de las principales ciudades de Ucrania.
"Si nuestros puentes se derrumban, conseguiremos salir de esta situación, pero su pueblo también lo notará… Se trata de la máxima escalada de esta guerra", dijo Zelenski a los periodistas.
Rusia lleva desde la semana pasada atacando los puentes de Kiev con el objetivo de cortar las conexiones entre las dos partes de la capital y las rutas logísticas entre el centro y el este de Ucrania.
MERZ PIDE FIN DE UNA "GUERRA SIN SENTIDO" Zelenski dijo que el enviado estadounidense, Steve Witkoff, le había mandado un mensaje para instarle a reanudar las conversaciones trilaterales lo antes posible. Señaló que Ucrania estaba dispuesta a reunirse este mes y esperaba que Rusia se sumara, pero añadió que los aliados occidentales deben ejercer más presión sobre Moscú para poner fin a la guerra.
Más temprano en el día, durante la visita a la Academia de Ciencias, gravemente dañada, Merz hizo un llamamiento a Putin para que "ponga fin a esta guerra sin sentido".
"Estamos preparados para conversaciones, estamos preparados para debatir cómo poner fin a esta guerra, pero estos ataques bárbaros frente la población civil de Ucrania deben cesar", dijo el líder alemán.
El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Rusia dijo el sábado que Moscú seguiría atacando sistemáticamente objetivos en Ucrania en lo que calificó de ataques de represalia por los ataques ucranianos contra Rusia. Advirtió a los ciudadanos extranjeros y al personal diplomático que no viajaran a Ucrania.
(1 dólar = 0,8887 euros)

items.title: Eagles RT Lane Johnson inactive vs. Rams
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson was listed as inactive for Sunday's game against the visiting Los Angeles Rams.
items.body:
Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson was listed as inactive for Sunday's game against the visiting Los Angeles Rams.
Johnson was given a game designation as questionable earlier Sunday due to personal reasons before the Eagles ruled him out 90 minutes prior to kickoff.
Philadelphia (2-1) is without six starters in all: Johnson, wide receiver DeVonta Smith, tight end Dallas Goedert, left guard Landon Dickerson, linebacker Zack Baun and safety Marcus Epps. Wideout Hollywood Brown, offensive tackle Fred Johnson and quarterback Cole Payton also were listed as inactive.
Rookie tackle Markel Bell started in place of Johnson.
Johnson, who turned 36 in May, told reporters in the summer that the 2026 season probably would be his last, citing priorities and his parents' health among his reasons.
The two-time first-team All-Pro reportedly was mulling retirement following a 2025 campaign that saw him sit out the final seven games of the regular season and the team's NFC wild-card loss to the San Francisco 49ers due to a Lisfranc injury.
Johnson is a two-time Super Bowl champion and six-time Pro Bowl selection. He has started all three games this season and 171 in his career since Philadelphia drafted him with the No. 4 overall pick in 2013.
As for the Rams (1-2), star defensive end Aaron Donald joined tight end Colby Parkinson, cornerbacks Cam Lampkin and Jaylen Watson, offensive lineman Bill Murray, wide receiver C.J. Daniels and quarterback Ty Simpson (emergency third QB) as inactive for the contest.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Britain's Green Party votes to class Zionism as a form of racism
items.author: David Milliken
items.creator: David Milliken
items.summary: Britain's Green Party voted on Sunday to class Zionism as a form of racism, drawing criticism from British Jews and from the Israeli government which said it now viewed the party as "a body that gives legitimacy to terrorism".
items.body:
Britain's Green Party voted on Sunday to class Zionism as a form of racism, drawing criticism from British Jews and from the Israeli government which said it now viewed the party as "a body that gives legitimacy to terrorism".
The party – which received 6% of the vote in national elections in 2024 – said it regarded Zionism as "an ethnonationalist political project" and repeated its call for Britain's Labour government to end all arms trade with Israel.
"The motion also restates the Green Party's backing for the right to self-determination and calls for the establishment of a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine," the party said in a statement.
The definition of Zionism – which inspired the foundation of the modern state of Israel in the 20th century – and what it implies for the rights of non-Jews in Israel and neighbouring territory, is contentious. Jewish groups sometimes define it as a right to Jewish self-determination.
The Green Party motion passed by a majority of 1,022 to 813 despite opposition from many senior figures. Party leader Zack Polanski, who is seeking election to Parliament on Thursday in former Prime Minister Keir Starmer's now-vacant London constituency, did not vote.
The result was condemned by British Jewish groups.
"The Green Party has made antisemitism party policy and become a racist party," the Movement for Progressive Judaism said, adding that the support of some Jews for the motion did not mean it would not be used to discriminate against others.
Israeli foreign minister Gideon Sa’ar has decided to declare Polanski barred from entering Israel, the foreign ministry said in a post on X Sunday.
It said the Green Party motion "constitutes a clear antisemitic text according to the IHRA (International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance) definition, as it denies the Jewish people’s right to self-determination," the ministry said.
Mothin Ali, deputy leader of the Green Party and a supporter of the motion, told Sky News on Saturday that the heavy Palestinian death toll in Israel's conflict with Hamas – which followed the Palestinian militant group's deadly 2023 attack on an Israeli music festival – was the key context for the vote.
"The motion defines Zionism quite clearly. It defines it as an ethnonationalist movement. It defines it as ethnic cleansing. It defines it as genocide," Ali said.
Britain's government views Israeli settlers' actions in the West Bank as [USN:L8N45007X TEXT:"amounting to ethnic cleansing"] but has said courts must decide if other Israeli actions qualify as genocide.
Israel – which rejects claims of ethnic cleansing and genocide – called on Sunday for other British political parties to condemn the Green Party vote. "The Greens have adopted not only the green of Hamas, but also its ideology: the elimination of the State of Israel through armed struggle," it said.
Polanski and other senior Green Party figures said they would "continue to call out the heinous crimes of the Netanyahu government," and that "there is no conflict between supporting the rights of Palestinians and the rights of Jewish people."
items.raw_description: Britain's Green Party voted on Sunday to class Zionism as a form of racism, drawing criticism from British Jews and from the Israeli government which said it now viewed the party as "a body that gives legitimacy to terrorism".

items.title: Iran's oil minister resigns for personal reasons, state media reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned for personal reasons, and Hamid Bovard, chief executive of the government-owned National Iranian Oil Company, will be acting minister, state media said on Sunday.
items.body:
Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned for personal reasons, and Hamid Bovard, chief executive of the government-owned National Iranian Oil Company, will be acting minister, state media said on Sunday.
Mohsen Paknejad, oil minister of the OPEC member country since August 2024, resigned as the seven-month-old war between Iran and the US has [USN:L6N45K0UX TEXT:"put pressure"] on the country's economy.
Mehdi Tabatabaei, communications deputy in the president's office, told state TV that Paknejad resigned for personal reasons "a long time ago" and his resignation was accepted by President Masoud Pezeshkian at Paknejad's insistence.
"With acceptance of Mohsen Paknejad's resignation by Dr. Pezeshkian, Hamid Bovard has been appointed as acting oil minister", Tabatabaei said earlier on Sunday, according to state media.
Before news of his resignation, Paknejad was quoted by state media as saying "revenues of the oil that we have sold are still coming and that will continue God willing".

items.title: Valentino unveils corset tops and chunky jewellery at fashion show in 19th-century Paris library
items.author: Helen Reid
items.creator: Helen Reid
items.summary: Valentino showed colourful corset tops, lace skirts and chunky gold necklaces on Sunday in a fashion show creative director Alessandro Michele dubbed "Antibiblioteca", set in the iconic reading room of the 19th-century Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève in Paris.
items.body:
Valentino showed colourful corset tops, lace skirts and chunky gold necklaces on Sunday in a fashion show creative director Alessandro Michele dubbed "Antibiblioteca", set in the iconic reading room of the 19th-century Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève in Paris.
On a sun-drenched afternoon, celebrities arrived each clutching a book which they showed off to the cameras and a large crowd of assembled fans. Guests including actors Alexander Skarsgard and Cynthia Erivo, American stylist Law Roach, and Chinese model Yidan Huang took their seats at long oak reading tables dotted with green lamps, under the library's iron latticework ceiling arches.
Michele has led the Roman [USN:L8N3YK19Q TEXT:"fashion house"] since March 2024 and is under pressure to revive sales at the brand that swung to a €103 million [USN:S8N40Y041 TEXT:"loss"] last year as revenues fell 15%. He was previously creative director at Gucci for eight years where his maximalist aesthetic and gender-fluid, eccentric designs like fur-lined loafers [USN:L8N32K398 TEXT:"reinvigorated"] the brand and boosted sales.
Models prowled along the library stacks in tight silk corset tops in bright blue, yellow, or hot pink, paired with skirts in contrasting colours. Dresses were strapless too, with the final look a floor-length Valentino red number with a giant black bow. Lace skirts and shirts had ostrich-feather hems.
Jewellery was chunky and colourful, with elaborate, baroque gold necklaces and giant pearl earrings. Women and men wore cross-body handbags or held rectangular clutches with studs and sequins.
Men wore half-buttoned double-breasted jackets or sequinned shirts, sporting tinted sunglasses and bright baseball caps with "VILLAIN TEEN" printed on them.
In June Valentino's shareholders — Qatar-backed Mayhoola, which owns 70% of the company, and French luxury group Kering, which holds the remaining 30% — committed additional financial support for 2026 after debt increased. Kering has options to increase its ownership to 100% before 2029.

items.title: Jonathan Taylor, Colts rush past injury-riddled Commanders
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns and the Indianapolis Colts pulled away in the fourth quarter to record a 30-13 victory over the undermanned Washington Commanders on Sunday in London.
items.body:
Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns and the Indianapolis Colts pulled away in the fourth quarter to record a 30-13 victory over the undermanned Washington Commanders on Sunday in London.
Taylor scored on a pair of 5-yard runs, enabling Indianapolis (2-2) to overcome a quick 6-0 deficit. He finished with 95 yards on 20 carries as the Colts made the most of their 257 yards.
Quarterback Daniel Jones shrugged off a pair of early turnovers to complete 19 of 34 passes for 143 yards and an interception. He also added the clinching score by running 5 yards on 3rd-and-2 for a touchdown with 11:38 left in the game that made it a two-touchdown margin.
Washington (1-3) played most of the day with rookie Athan Kaliakmanis at quarterback after starter Marcus Mariota suffered a right knee injury in the first quarter and wasn't able to return.
Kaliakmanis completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Mariota connected on 3 of 4 passes for 46 yards and rushed for 35 yards on one carry before departing.
The Commanders got off to a quick start, getting a strip-sack on Indianapolis' second play and converting that into Drew Stevens' 31-yard field goal just 2:03 into the game. Stevens made it 6-0 on a 29-yard field goal from Stevens with 6:21 left in the quarter.
That lead held until the Colts, who managed only 33 yards on their first four possessions, finally found traction. Taylor's first touchdown run with 3:23 remaining in the half put them ahead for good and Spencer Shrader's 48-yard field goal made it 10-6 at the break.
Taylor scored again at the 12:45 mark of the third quarter, four plays after Kaliakmanis tossed an interception. But Kaliakmanis responded with a 47-yard touchdown pass to Traylon Burks with 10:39 left in the period.
Shrader drilled a 52-yarder with 7:03 remaining in the third for a 20-13 advantage. In the fourth quarter, he added a 44-yarder with 5:48 on the clock to cap the scoring.
--Field Level Media

items.title: France/Lycées Entre 400 et 500 établissements encore fermés lundi - ministre
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Entre 400 et 500 lycées devraient rester complètement ou partiellement fermés lundi en France, sur un total de 3.700, soit des chiffres similaires à vendredi, a déclaré dimanche le ministre de l'Education Edouard Geffray, signe que la mobilisation des lycéens ne faiblit pas.
items.body:
Entre 400 et 500 lycées devraient rester complètement ou partiellement fermés lundi en France, sur un total de 3.700, soit des chiffres similaires à vendredi, a déclaré dimanche le ministre de l'Education Edouard Geffray, signe que la mobilisation des lycéens ne faiblit pas.
"Il y avait entre 400 et 500 lycées qui ont suspendu leurs cours vendredi et il y en aura probablement autant lundi mais avec une reprise partielle et progressive des cours qui va se mettre en place", a-t-il précisé sur France 2.
Edouard Geffray a tenté de calmer vendredi la mobilisation dans les lycées en France en recevant les représentants de syndicats étudiants, qui ont fait part de leur déception et appelé à [USN:L8N45O1H4 TEXT:"poursuivre leur mouvement"].
Tout en se désolidarisant des violences ayant éclaté en marge des blocages d'établissements, ils ont appelé à des rassemblements mardi 6 octobre et seront rejoints par plusieurs confédérations syndicales dont la CGT.
Les élèves qui bloquent les lycées dénoncent notamment des classes surpeuplées, le manque d'enseignants ou encore la vétusté des bâtiments, attribuant ces problèmes à des années de sous-investissement dans le secteur de l'enseignement public.
Dans une lettre adressée à Edouard Geffray ainsi qu'à d'autres ministres, le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu demande à ce que "cinq chantiers" soient engagés "pour répondre aux difficultés des lycéens et des personnels".
Parmi les chantiers énumérés, celui que Sébastien Lecornu considère comme le plus important est la nécessité de donner des "suites visibles à la parole de lycéens".
"Chaque proposition recevra une réponse motivée, avec une échéance lorsqu'elle sera retenue", a déclaré le Premier ministre, demandant à ses ministres des "premières décisions, leur coût, leur financement et leur calendrier" d'ici la fin du mois.
ACCÉLÉRER L'EXAMEN DU PROJET DE LOI "CASSEUR-PAYEUR" "La confiance se rétablira lorsque chacun pourra constater ce qui change dans son lycée", a encore dit Sébastien Lecornu, qui adopte aussi un ton de fermeté par rapport aux violences qui ont émaillé les blocages.
"Avec le ministre de l'Intérieur et le garde des Sceaux, nous allons accélérer l'examen du projet de loi "casseur-payeur", pour mieux faire supporter aux auteurs de dégradations le coût des dommages causés", a-t-il ajouté.
"La fermeté face aux violences et aux tentatives d'instrumentalisation doit aller de pair avec l'écoute des inquiétudes légitimes. Notre soutien va aux élèves et personnels agressés, aux policiers et gendarmes blessés."
Edouard Geffray a précisé dimanche que 24 établissements scolaires avaient été "incendiés ou saccagés" et que "78 personnels" de l'éducation nationale avaient été blessés depuis le début du mouvement.
Depuis lundi, environ 5.000 personnes, pour la plupart des adolescents, ont été interpellées dans tout le pays et des dizaines d'autres ont été blessées.
Le mobilisation lycéenne est partie le 18 septembre d'établissements en banlieue parisienne [USN:L6N45P01N TEXT:"défavorisés"] avant de s'étendre au reste du pays.

items.title: イラン、米の回答に立場表明　再攻撃なら対応と外相
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ドバイ ４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ドバイ ４日 ロイター] - イラン外務省のバガイ報道官は４日、ホルムズ海峡再開に関する直近の提案への米国の回答に対するイランの大まかな立場を仲介国を通じて米国側に伝えたと述べた。また、イランが米国の制裁緩和と引き換えに、国際原子力機関（ＩＡＥＡ）による核施設の査察受け入れを提案したとの情報を否定し、米国とは核協議に入っていないと説明した。

イランは９月の国連総会期間中に、条件が満たされればホルムズ海峡を再開し、７日以内に通常の船舶航行を回復させるとする提案を示した。米国は９月下旬に仲介役のカタールを通じてこの提案に回答した。

バガイ氏は、「米国側の提案は、特に核問題について、従来の立場とほぼ変わらない。われわれは、現段階で重視するのはホルムズ海峡の問題であり、同海峡の安全を取り戻すには米国が明確な措置を講じる必要があると伝えた」と述べた。米政府に伝える追加の論点がまだ残っていると説明した。

イラン側の交渉責任者を務めるガリバフ国会議長は４日、６月の暫定合意で定めたイラン側の７つの条件が満たされるまで、ホルムズ海峡は再開しないと述べた。国営メディアが伝えた。

アラグチ外相は４日、イラン駐在の各国大使や外交官に対し、米国が外交を選ぶことを望むと述べた。ただ、米国が再び軍事行動を選んだ場合は対応する用意があると警告し、「彼らが再び軍事的解決に向かうなら、われわれは以前より準備が整っており、自衛のために必要なあらゆる行動を取る」と述べた。

ロイターは１日、関係筋の話として、米国が大規模な軍事攻撃を再開した場合に備え、イランがより広範で強力な対応を準備していると報じた。

イラン軍の報道官は４日、ファルス通信に対し、ミサイルの射程を延ばす方針だと語った。

items.title: Woman at center of Cornell rape allegations targeted with threats, lawyer says
items.author: Nolan Mccaskill
items.creator: Nolan Mccaskill
items.summary: Thomas Giuffra told CNN that people have threatened to silence or harm her if she does not withdraw her civil lawsuit alleging that several members of a fraternity drugged and raped her in 2024.
items.body:
The woman who has alleged that she was drugged and raped by Cornell University students has been the target of threats, her lawyer said on Sunday.
Thomas Giuffra, who represents the woman identified as "Jane Doe," told CNN that people have threatened to silence or harm her if she does not withdraw her [USN:L1N45O0OO TEXT:"civil lawsuit"] alleging that several members of a Cornell fraternity drugged and raped her in 2024.
"She's received multiple threats," Giuffra said on CNN's "State of the Union."
Giuffra said he had also been threatened.
"I'm not afraid of these people," he said. "But the threats, the abuse to protect what's going on, the status quo — these guys are disgusting. They should stay in their mother's basement and stay out of the world."
Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said in a video message on Saturday that the university [USN:L1N45P06O TEXT:"will examine"] the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following the [USN:L6N45O14X TEXT:"outcry"] over the school's handling of the rape allegations.
"At their best, these organizations can provide students with friendship, belonging, mentorship and a powerful sense of community," he said. "But being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."
Since the lawsuit was filed last month, prosecutors in Tompkins County, New York, have been criticized for their initial handling of the allegations in 2024. New York Governor Kathy Hochul last week named state Attorney General Letitia James as [USN:L1N45O00M TEXT:"special prosecutor"] to look into the case.
US President Donald Trump, a critic of James for years, lambasted the decision to appoint her. "And I feel badly for whoever she's looking at because they won't get a fair shake," Trump told reporters on Friday.
Asked about Trump's comment, Giuffra said the case shouldn't be politicized. "It has nothing to do with politics," Giuffra said.

items.title: Commanders QB Marcus Mariota injured vs. Colts
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Washington Commanders lost quarterback Marcus Mariota to a right knee injury in the first quarter of their 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London on Sunday.
items.body:
The Washington Commanders lost quarterback Marcus Mariota to a right knee injury in the first quarter of their 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London on Sunday.
Mariota was injured after being sacked by Laiatu Latu on a third-and-goal play. Mariota appeared to get his leg twisted under him while going down. He left the field under his own power and later went to the locker room. He was ruled out at halftime.
Mariota completed 3-of-4 passes for 46 yards and ran once for 35 yards before departing the game. He guided Washington (1-3) to field goals on its first two possessions as he filled in for starting quarterback Jayden Daniels (left elbow).
Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, a seventh-round pick out of Rutgers, replaced Mariota and became the first quarterback from the 2026 draft class to take a snap in a regular-season game.
Kaliakmanis finished 15-of-33 passing for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception.
In other injury news, Commanders return specialist Jaylin Lane was carted off the field after suffering what appeared to be a serious injury to his lower left leg.
On Sunday, he returned three kickoffs for 80 yards and two punts for a combined 17 yards.
The Commanders began the game without top receiver Terry McLaurin, who suffered a hamstring injury in practice on Friday.
--Field Level Media

items.title: イエメン暫定政権、フーシ派に対する大規模軍事作戦開始　全土掌握目指す
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Mohammed Ghobari　Timour Azhari

[アデン ４日 ロイター] - サウジアラビアが支援するイエメン暫定政権の指導者であるアリーミ大統領評議会議長は４日、親イラン武装組織フーシ派に対する大規模な軍事作戦の開始を発表した。フーシ派が支配する地域を奪還して全土の掌握を目指す。

アリーミ氏は演説で「本日、共和国の残りの領土を奪還し、国家とその機関の権限を国土全体に及ぼすための軍事作戦の開始を宣言する」と述べた。
items.body:
Mohammed Ghobari　Timour Azhari

[アデン ４日 ロイター] - サウジアラビアが支援するイエメン暫定政権の指導者であるアリーミ大統領評議会議長は４日、親イラン武装組織フーシ派に対する大規模な軍事作戦の開始を発表した。フーシ派が支配する地域を奪還して全土の掌握を目指す。

アリーミ氏は演説で「本日、共和国の残りの領土を奪還し、国家とその機関の権限を国土全体に及ぼすための軍事作戦の開始を宣言する」と述べた。 軍や治安部隊、全ての軍事組織に対し、承認済みの計画に基づき割り当てられた任務の遂行を始めるよう命じたと述べた。 

軍報道官はその後、フーシ派に武装解除を呼びかけた。

２０２２年に合意した停戦はおおむね守られてきたが、今年に入り、イラン戦争が波及し、フーシ派がサウジの船舶や石油インフラへのミサイル・ドローン（無人機）攻撃を始めた。

アリーミ氏は演説で、フーシ派が紛争を沈静化させる取り組みに応じず、さらに緊張を激化させたと非難し、事態打開の可能性が尽きたため、攻撃の開始を決めたと説明した。

サウジは１５年、フーシ派によって首都サヌアを追われた、国際的に承認された政府を支援するため、アラブ連合軍を率いてイエメンの内戦に介入した。

アリーミ氏はサウジの支援に謝意を示した上で、地域の同盟国や国際的パートナーに対し、イエメン暫定政権とその軍への支援を呼びかけた。

一方、フーシ派は４日、サウジの首都リヤドや東部クライスにある国有石油会社サウジアラムコの施設を弾道ミサイルとドローンで攻撃し、大規模な火災を引き起こしたと発表した。過去１２時間の間にサウジ主導の有志連合軍がイエメン国内で５０回に及ぶ空爆やミサイル攻撃を行ったことへの報復だとした。フーシ派は前日も、リヤドのアラムコの施設を弾道ミサイルと無人機で攻撃したと発表していた。

サウジ側から直ちに確認は得られていない。 

中東地域や西側の当局者はロイターに、サウジがフーシ派に対する軍事作戦を計画していると述べていた。 

サウジの準備状況を知る関係者６人によると、米国は既にイエメンでのサウジの作戦を支援するため情報を提供している。中東地域や欧州の一部の国も、主に防衛目的の軍事支援をサウジに提供している。

フーシ派は９月の奇襲攻撃で戦略的要衝のバベルマンデブ海峡周辺を掌握して以降、地上戦で主導権を維持している。

items.title: Presidencia Brasil se definiría en segunda vuelta, ventaja de Bolsonaro sobre Lula se achica
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga
items.summary: La ventaja del senador Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se seguía achicando el domingo tras el recuento de aproximadamente el 90% de los votos, y la encuestadora Datafolha pronosticó que la presidencia de Brasil se definirá en una segunda vuelta a fin de este mes.
items.body:
La ventaja del senador Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se seguía achicando el domingo tras el recuento de aproximadamente el 90% de los votos, y la encuestadora Datafolha pronosticó que la presidencia de Brasil se definirá en una segunda vuelta a fin de este mes.
Bolsonaro, de 45 años e hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, que aspira a devolver al poder al movimiento de derecha de su padre, aventajaba a Lula, de 80 años y que busca un cuarto mandato no consecutivo, tras una campaña dominada por escándalos de corrupción, inquietud económica y acusaciones de injerencia estadounidense.
Con el 90,15% de los votos escrutados, Bolsonaro superaba a Lula con el 48,05% de los sufragios frente al 43,96% del presidente.
Los sondeos privados previos a la votación proyectaban que el mandatario iba a imponerse en la primera vuelta por 3 puntos porcentuales.
Si ningún candidato obtiene más del 50% de los sufragios válidos, los dos más votados se enfrentarán en la segunda vuelta el 25 de octubre. Las encuestas muestran a Lula y Bolsonaro prácticamente empatados en caso de un balotaje.
Las cifras indicaban que los estados del sur, que se inclinan por Bolsonaro, comunicaban los resultados más rápidamente, mientras que los votos del bastión de Lula en el noreste se recontaban más lentamente.
Analistas declararon a Reuters que creían que Bolsonaro estaba recibiendo "votos castigo" de personas que estaban en contra de Lula más que a favor del senador.
Una victoria de Bolsonaro prolongaría la ola de triunfos en América Latina de candidatos de derecha alineados con Donald Trump, mientras que la reelección de Lula podría suponer un dolor de cabeza para Washington, que ha tenido enfrentamientos con su gobierno en materia de comercio y seguridad.
A pesar de la creciente preocupación por la salud fiscal de Brasil y su lento crecimiento económico, la campaña ofreció poco debate político sustancial, ya que los candidatos principales se ausentaron de los principales debates televisados.
Si bien los sondeos realizados hasta el sábado indicaban que Lula probablemente lideraría la primera vuelta pero no evitaría una segunda, Bolsonaro declaró a periodistas en Río de Janeiro que confiaba en ganar la presidencia el domingo, citando la frustración de los votantes con su principal rival.
Bolsonaro dijo que apuesta por "un voto de protesta de personas que, de otro modo, votarían por otro candidato pero se oponen a Lula". "Espero que sea suficiente para asegurar la victoria en la primera vuelta".
Thaise Lima, una abogada de 41 años que se dirigía a votar en São Paulo, afirmó que su principal objetivo era sacar del poder al Partido de los Trabajadores de Lula.
"No creo que Flavio sea el mejor candidato, pero quizá decida votar por él", dijo, y añadió que le hubiera gustado que el psiquiatra y escritor Augusto Cury fuera un candidato más viable.
INTERFERENCIA EXTERNA Por otro lado, los aliados de Lula han advertido que el Gobierno de Trump podría negarse a reconocer los resultados si el líder de izquierda gana, señalando un intento frustrado de enviar funcionarios estadounidenses a Brasil.
"Lo que está en juego es el futuro de Brasil", dijo Lula tras votar en Sao Bernardo do Campo, en el estado de Sao Paulo.
Trump no ha respaldado formalmente a ningún candidato, aunque recibió al senador Flávio Bolsonaro en la Casa Blanca y lo elogió públicamente.
"Confiamos en nuestro presidente Lula, que luchará por la soberanía nacional", afirmó Pedro Palacio, de 45 años, que votaba en Brasilia junto a su esposa, Andreia, y sus dos hijos y dos perros, todos ellos ataviados con prendas en apoyo al presidente.
Hasta la tarde del domingo, la elección transcurrió con normalidad, según declaró en rueda de prensa Kassio Nunes Marques, titular del tribunal electoral de Brasil.
"Los equipos que monitorean los riesgos internacionales no han identificado riesgo alguno", afirmó.
Reuters informó el miércoles que funcionarios de inteligencia brasileños informaron a una delegación francesa y alemana sobre una supuesta interferencia de Estados Unidos y Rusia antes de las elecciones. Estados Unidos ha rechazado las acusaciones de interferencia en los asuntos de Brasil.
A pesar de la disminución de la desigualdad y el desempleo, Lula ha tenido dificultades para ganarse a los votantes que se enfrentan al aumento del costo de la vida, a las elevadas deudas de los hogares y la creciente actividad de las bandas criminales.
Bolsonaro ha intentado sacar provecho de la preocupación por el costo de la vida, mientras que Lula ha tomado medidas para prohibir las apuestas en línea, a las que se culpa de alimentar la deuda y, a medida que la contienda se estrechaba, amplió las ayudas sociales y anunció la condonación de deudas para las familias.
El aumento del gasto y una deuda pública superior al 82% del PIB han avivado preocupaciones fiscales que el próximo presidente de Brasil podría tener que abordar. El Gobierno redujo sus previsiones de crecimiento económico para este año y el próximo a apenas un 2,0% y un 2,3%, respectivamente.
"He votado para que Brasil vuelva a crecer", afirmó Marciano de Souza e Silva, un funcionario de 52 años de Brasilia y antiguo votante de Lula que se ha desplazado hacia la derecha, votando a Jair Bolsonaro en 2018 y 2022 y a su hijo el domingo.
"El mejor programa social es aquel que anima a la gente a crear empresas, a generar riqueza real", afirmó.
Más allá del debate sobre políticas públicas, un escándalo que rodea al ahora desaparecido Banco Master ha salpicado a gran parte de la clase política brasileña y reavivando la indignación pública por la corrupción.
Daniel Vorcaro, el antiguo director del banco, fue arrestado a principios de este año por un presunto fraude multimillonario. La investigación ha indagado sobre los vínculos de Vorcaro con figuras que van desde el magistrado de la corte suprema Alexandre de Moraes hasta el propio Flávio Bolsonaro, quien está siendo investigado por blanqueo de dinero relacionado con el caso.
El senador ha negado haber cometido irregularidades, aunque confirmó haber recibido millones de dólares de Vorcaro para financiar una película sobre su padre.

items.title: Yemeni government launches offensive to seize all areas from Iran-backed Houthis
items.author: Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: Despite the preparations for a counteroffensive, the Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground, weeks after seizing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive that saw government forces collapse.
items.body:
Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday it was launching a major military campaign to recapture all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis .
The government’s armed forces would press the offensive “until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia,” Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address. A military spokesman later called on the Houthis to lay down their weapons.
The Houthis, known formally as Ansar Allah, have held Yemen’s capital Sanaa and vast parts of the northwest, where most of the population live, since 2014. They have so far withstood a series of attacks over the years by Saudi Arabia, the UAE and their Western allies, and have updated their weaponry with the help of Iran.
The movement launched a surprise offensive last month which captured the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait and some 150 km (90 miles) of coast on the Red Sea in a matter of weeks, giving the Houthis new leverage over the international shipping route.
That advance also opened a new front in the wider US-Israeli war launched in February against Iran, to which Tehran’s responses included choking oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz , to the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.
HOUTHIS SAY THEY STRUCK SAUDI ARABIA As the Yemeni government, known as the Presidential Leadership Council, made its announcement, the Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia.
They claimed the attacks caused major fires and were in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.
Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all chances of de-escalating the conflict had been exhausted.
He thanked Saudi Arabia for its support and called on Yemen's regional allies and international partners to support PLC forces and institutions.
Regional and western officials had told Reuters earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to [USN:L8N45M1W0 TEXT:"launch an assault"] on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground.
NEW FRONT IN MIDEAST WAR The US is already providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters.
The United States’ war on Iran has decimated a layer of Iranian military and political leadership, but has also entangled Washington in a new engagement in the Middle East and depleted crucial military hardware.
Yemen has been mired in conflict for years, with an array of local armed groups and factions backed by competing regional and international actors.
After a popular uprising that was part of the Arab Spring movements in 2011, the Houthis, an armed group of Zaidi Shi’ite Muslims, captured Sanaa.
The Saudi-backed PLC, which is also recognised by the United Nations, has since the Houthi takeover controlled the south and east of the country, based in the former South Yemen capital of Aden.
Saudi Arabia entered Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the PLC, but failed to defeat the Houthis.
A truce agreed between the warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.
HOUTHIS ON FRONT FOOT The Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground since seizing control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in their lightning offensive last month that saw government forces collapse.
Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that has assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.
In the last 48 hours, the Houthis have also made gains against government and local forces on strategic hilltops near Yemen's Taiz, military sources said, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden on the southern coast.
Houthi control over the Taiz-Aden road would lead to an effective siege of the city, Yemen's third-largest, inhabited by hundreds of thousands of civilians and where thousands of government forces are also stationed.
The city is important not just for its strategic location; Alimi is from the region, and a siege of Taiz would amplify an already-dire humanitarian situation in the country.
Three in four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week.

items.title: Can America Break China’s Grip on Rare Earths?
items.summary: China spent decades building a dominant position across rare-earth mining, processing and magnet manufacturing, leaving the US dependent on a foreign supply chain for materials essential to everything from vehicles and wind turbines to electronics and defense systems. MP Materials is now trying to rebuild that chain domestically, moving from its Mountain Pass mine in California into refining. But catching up will take more than finding minerals: the US still faces higher costs, limited processing capacity, opaque pricing and a Chinese lead that industry experts say took roughly 25 years to build. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Votação chega ao fim em eleição polarizada entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
items.author: Eduardo Simões
items.creator: Eduardo Simões
items.summary: As quase 500 mil seções eleitorais espalhadas pelo Brasil começaram a ser fechadas às 17h deste domingo, dando início à expectativa para a divulgação do resultado em uma disputa pela Presidência da República acirrada e polarizada entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
items.body:
As quase 500 mil seções eleitorais espalhadas pelo Brasil começaram a ser fechadas às 17h deste domingo, dando início à expectativa para a divulgação do resultado em uma disputa pela Presidência da República acirrada e polarizada entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
Marcada por polêmicas envolvendo desde o Judiciário até a padroeira do Brasil, passando por denúncias generalizadas de corrupção e temores de interferência externa, a campanha eleitoral para presidente chegou ao primeiro turno com a disputa totalmente em aberto entre os dois principais candidatos.
Lula e Flávio votaram no começo da manhã e manifestaram confiança na vitória.
Ao votar em uma escola em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), Lula fez um apelo para que os eleitores com mais de 70 anos comparecessem às urnas e reafirmou que o que estava em jogo nas eleições era a escolha entre o "fortalecimento do regime democrático e a barbárie".
Flávio Bolsonaro votou em uma escola em Vila Isabel, no Rio de Janeiro, pouco após a abertura das urnas, e disse que esperava vencer já no primeiro turno. "As nossas pesquisas internas mostram que a gente ultrapassou no primeiro turno já faz algum tempo", declarou. "Espero que seja suficiente para dar vitória no primeiro turno."
As pesquisas de intenção de voto divulgadas no sábado, no entanto, apontam para uma nova rodada de votação, que aconteceria em 25 de outubro.
Para a eleição acabar neste domingo, é preciso que um dos candidatos conquiste mais de 50% dos votos válidos, quando são desconsiderados os votos brancos e nulos.
Levantamentos do Datafolha e da Quaest colocaram Lula e Flávio em empate técnico no primeiro turno nos votos válidos, com vantagem numérica do atual presidente de 3 pontos na primeira e de 1 ponto na segunda. Uma outra pesquisa, do MDA, colocou Lula com 47,8% dos votos válidos contra 42,1% de Flávio.
O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou confiar em um processo tranquilo de votação: "Amanhecemos o dia hoje com a segurança de que as eleições vão transcorrer na maior normalidade", disse, ao votar em Brasília no início da manhã.
Os mais de 158,7 milhões de brasileiros aptos a votar puderam ir às seções eleitorais ao longo do dia -- as urnas abriram às 8h e fecharam às 17h pelo horário de Brasília -- após meses de embates muitas vezes em nível pessoal de cada lado, em que as propostas para governar o país pelos próximos quatro anos não foram protagonistas.
A campanha chegou ao fim sem que Lula e Flávio tenham se enfrentado diretamente. No debate da TV Bandeirantes, ambos decidiram não ir, deixando os púlpitos vazios com seus nomes para serem criticados por Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão) e Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), que estavam presentes. Romeu Zema (Novo) completa a lista dos outros candidatos cujos partidos têm representação no Congresso, mas cujas intenções de voto jamais se aproximaram da dos dois líderes.
Já o debate da TV Globo, que tradicionalmente encerra as campanhas, acabou sendo [USN:L1N45N18V TEXT:"cancelado"] após uma série de decisões judiciais e da desistência de última hora de Flávio, filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro -- que está atualmente em prisão domiciliar após ser condenado por tentativa de golpe de Estado. Lula havia dito dias antes que não compareceria.
Nunes Marques disse esperar que candidatos acionem a Justiça com questionamentos relacionados às eleições, mas frisou, em entrevista coletiva nesta tarde, que a votação está transcorrendo com normalidade e transparência. Segundo ele, as urnas estão funcionando normalmente e não houve necessidade de votação manual em nenhum ponto do país.
TEMOR DE INTERFERÊNCIA A eleição também ocorre em meio a renovados temores sobre uma possível interferência estrangeira na eleição presidencial brasileira. A Reuters [USN:L6N45M0VR TEXT:"revelou"] na última semana que autoridades francesas e alemãs ouviram de membros da Agência Brasileira de Inteligência (Abin) que já estariam acontecendo tentativas de interferência dos Estados Unidos e da Rússia no pleito.
O diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, afirmou neste domingo que a corporação já abriu investigação para apurar suposto esquema de financiamento de uma agenda de extrema-direita no Brasil pelo governo norte-americano de Donald Trump que teria entre os objetivos interferir nas eleições brasileiras.
A investigação foi solicitada pela Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) na quinta-feira e teve como base reportagem publicada no jornal inglês The Guardian, segundo a qual o Departamento de Estado norte-americano teria destinado US$1 milhão de um fundo ligado aos direitos humanos e à democracia para um programa chamado "Combate ao Lawfare e à Censura no Brasil".
Nunes Marques enfatizou, no entanto, que o TSE não identificou nenhum indicativo de interferência estrangeira nas eleições. “Equipes que monitoram riscos internacionais não apontam qualquer tipo de risco”, afirmou.
Na última quinta-feira, a embaixada dos EUA no Brasil [USN:L6N45O0XD TEXT:"anunciou"] a suspensão dos serviços consulares a partir da sexta-feira, alegando preocupações não especificadas de segurança. Além disso, a embaixada pediu aos seus funcionários que trabalhassem de casa na sexta após uma ameaça. A embaixadora da Austrália também anunciou o fechamento da representação diplomática do país em Brasília citando o alerta norte-americano.
A medida foi criticada pelo presidente do PT, Edinho Silva, que viu tentativa do governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de influenciar a opinião pública brasileira. Neste domingo, no entanto, Nunes Marques ponderou que a iniciativa seria usual no caso de eleições acirradas, e citou que teria acontecido o fechamento de embaixadas também durante o último pleito na Colômbia.
A relação com os EUA e com Trump foi um dos principais marcadores da diferença entre Lula e Flávio. Enquanto o presidente alertou o homólogo norte-americano publicamente a não interferir no Brasil, o senador procurou mostrar proximidade com Trump, inclusive visitando-o na Casa Branca.
"É uma relação tensa porque o Brasil não quer se ver dentro da zona de influência dos EUA. Tradicionalmente a nossa diplomacia é independente. O Lula acredita que, pela boa relação com a China, especialmente a comercial, que manter essa independência é fundamental", disse Leonardo Barreto, cofundador da Think Policy.
"O Flávio tenta fazer dos EUA uma espécie de fiador das eleições. A família Bolsonaro acredita que as eleições não são feitas em condições de liberdade. Desconfiança em relação a urna, meios de comunicação, administração do Judiciário. Buscam no apoio dos americanos uma espécie de pressão para garantir o mínimo de neutralidade das autoridades brasileiras, percebem nos americanos uma espécie de seguro", acrescentou.
BETS, STF E PADROEIRA Em meio a denúncias de corrupção como as do Banco Master e o escândalo do INSS, que atingiram tanto Flávio quanto o filho mais velho de Lula, além de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), a campanha também foi marcada pelo apelo do senador à imagem de seu pai, ao mesmo tempo em que buscava se mostrar mais moderado do que o ex-presidente, enquanto Lula seguiu batendo na tecla dos seus três mandatos na Presidência e lançando mão de medidas populares às vésperas do pleito.
Entre elas, o governo anunciou o reajuste de 15% nos benefícios do Bolsa Família, a edição de uma medida provisória para proibir casas de apostas online e o anúncio da intenção de distribuir gratuitamente pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) as chamadas canetas emagrecedoras, três medidas aprovadas pelo eleitorado, segundo as pesquisas de opinião.
Mas a polêmica que marcou a reta final da campanha ficou por conta de rumores de que Flávio retiraria de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil, o que foi negado com veemência pelo senador. Flávio classificou os boatos de "fake news", enquanto Lula disse que, enquanto for presidente, ninguém irá "avacalhar" com Nossa Senhora.
Além do presidente, os eleitores também escolherão neste domingo os governadores dos 26 Estados e do Distrito Federal, além de 54 dos 81 senadores e dos 513 deputados e dos integrantes das Assembleias Legislativas de 26 Estados e da Câmara Distrital do Distrito Federal.
A eleição para o Senado estará sob o foco, em um momento de pressão sobre ministros do STF, que podem sofrer impeachment pelos integrantes da Casa, e em um momento em que estão [USN:L6N45N0ZL TEXT:"vagas"] funções em órgãos reguladores, como o Banco Central, cujos nomes precisam ser aprovados pelos senadores.

items.title: OPEC+ agrees to keep November oil output targets steady
items.author: Ahmad Ghaddar, Alex Lawler, Olesya Astakhova
items.creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Alex Lawler, Olesya Astakhova
items.summary: OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production targets steady for November at a meeting on Sunday, the producer group said, in line with expectations that further output policy adjustments are unlikely until next year.
items.body:
OPEC+ agreed to keep oil production targets steady for November at a meeting on Sunday, the producer group said, in line with expectations that further output policy adjustments are unlikely until next year.
Seven core members of the group comprising the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia made the decision for November in a brief online meeting on Sunday. The core members are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman.
Gulf OPEC+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran , with exports fluctuating at 60% to 80% of normal levels in recent months.
"The OPEC+ group of seven kept their production ceilings unchanged, in line with market expectations. That said, despite rising flows through the Strait of Hormuz, their output levels remain well below quota," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo.
"Consequently, the oil market remains tight."
Oil prices had dropped on Friday after European leaders agreed to US President Donald Trump's request to release diesel reserves. Even so, Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel, up from about $73 before the Iran war started in late February.
OUTPUT HIKES HAVE BEEN LARGELY ON PAPER THIS YEAR The Iran war has also delayed the group's output [USN:L6N45O0QD TEXT:"capacity review"] — crucial to determine members’ 2027 output quotas — because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources told Reuters last week.
OPEC+ has been raising output targets for much of 2026 after years of production cuts, but most of the increases stayed on paper because of the Middle East conflict.
The seven core OPEC+ members pumped 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly 5 million bpd below prewar levels in February, OPEC data shows.
The seven hold their next meeting on November 1.
OPEC+ still has about 2 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members. It needs the result of the capacity review to decide how to distribute increases and any [USN:L6N43U0TI TEXT:"changes to output are unlikely"] before 2027, sources have said.
A separate OPEC+ ministerial group called the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC), which does not decide policy, also met on Sunday to review the market.

items.title: Brazil election headed to runoff, projection shows, as Bolsonaro lead narrows
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Luciana Magalhaes, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
items.summary: Senator Flavio Bolsonaro held a narrowing lead in the first round of Brazil's presidential election after more than half the votes were counted, with pollster Datafolha projecting that the election would proceed to a second vote.
items.body:
Senator Flavio Bolsonaro held a narrowing lead in the first round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, after more than half the votes were counted, with pollster Datafolha projecting that the election would proceed to a second vote.
Flavio, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who hopes to return his father's right-wing movement to power, was leading leftist [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva"], 80, who is seeking a fourth term, following a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling.
With nearly 85% of votes reported, Flavio led Lula with 48.47% of the votes to the president's 43.49%. A candidate must pass 50% in order to win outright in the first round.
Private surveys in the run up to the election had forecast Lula leading the first-round vote by around 3 percentage points.
The two leading candidates were expected to head into a second-round vote, Brazilian pollster Datafolha said. Surveys have shown Lula and Flavio polling roughly even in an October 25 runoff.
Early results showed southern states that lean to Bolsonaro reporting faster, while votes from Lula's northeast stronghold have been tallied more slowly.
Analysts told Reuters they believed Flavio was receiving "protest votes" of people voting against Lula rather than for the right-wing senator - votes they had been expected to save until a second round.
A victory for the senator would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's reelection could create a headache for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.
Despite growing worries over Brazil's public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"meager policy debate"], as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.
UNDECIDED VOTERS While polls right up until Saturday showed Lula would likely lead the first round but not avoid a runoff, Flavio told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was confident he could win the presidency in the first round, citing voters' frustration with his chief opponent.
Flavio was counting on "a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula," he said. "I hope it’s enough to secure a victory in the first round."
Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Lula's Workers' Party out of office.
"I don't think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes," she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.
Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Flavio despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.
OUTSIDE INTERFERENCE On the other hand, Lula's allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to [USN:L6N43R03C TEXT:"send US officials to Brazil"].
"What is at stake is the future of Brazil," Lula said after voting in Sao Bernardo do Campo, in Sao Paulo state.
Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.
"I'm a little worried about everything that's been happening recently, including internationally. I feel this election has had a lot of outside influence, more than in previous elections," said Cristiano, 34, a doctor in Brasilia who voted for Lula and preferred to withhold his surname.
"We are confident in our President Lula, who will fight for national sovereignty," said Pedro Palacio, 45, who was voting in Brasilia alongside his wife, Andreia, and their two sons and two dogs, all of whom wore outfits supporting the president.
As of Sunday afternoon, the election was proceeding normally, Brazil's electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said in a press conference.
“Teams monitoring international risks have not identified any risks whatsoever," he said.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on [USN:L1N45E08V TEXT:"alleged US and Russian interference"] before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs.
ECONOMIC HEADWINDS Despite [USN:L1N44111S TEXT:"falling inequality"] and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with high living costs, heavy household debt and the threat of street crime and more pervasive gang activity.
Flavio Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula has moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.
Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's next president will need to address. The government lowered its [USN:L1N45E0QC TEXT:"economic growth forecasts"] for this year and next to 2.0% and 2.3% respectively.
"I voted for Brazil to start growing again," said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia and former Lula voter who moved right, voting for Jair Bolsonaro in 2018 and 2022 and Flavio on Sunday.
"The best social program is one that encourages people to start businesses, to actually produce real wealth," he said.
SCANDAL-PLAGUED CAMPAIGNS Overshadowing the policy debate, a scandal surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil's political class and renewed public anger over corruption.
Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. The investigation has probed the banker's ties to figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to Flavio Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police.
The candidate has denied any wrongdoing, although he confirmed raising millions of dollars from Vorcaro to make a movie about his father.
The banker's connections to Moraes, widely perceived as a Lula ally, [USN:L6N44U1B6 TEXT:"plunged the court into crisis"] a month before the vote, creating fresh problems for the president. Moraes has said the case against him is politically motivated for his role in the [USN:L1N45711X TEXT:"conviction of the elder Bolsonaro"].
On Sunday, voters will also elect all 513 lower house members and two-thirds of the Senate, where some lawmakers have pushed to impeach Moraes.
Congress has gained greater influence in Brazilian politics since the impeachment of former President Dilma Rousseff, a Lula ally, in 2016, raising the stakes of those legislative races.

items.title: Éthiopie-La capitale du Tigré sous contrôle des forces gouvernementales
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont-elles déclaré dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord.
items.body:
Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont-elles déclaré dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord.
Les Forces de paix du Tigré, une milice pro-gouvernementale dit dans un message publié sur Facebook que ses combattants avaient pris le contrôle de Mekelle, la capitale du Tigré.
Une source proche de la milice avait auparavant dit à Reuters qu'elle était entrée dans le centre-ville samedi après-midi, suivie par l'armée éthiopienne.
Le Front populaire de libération du Tigré (TPLF), qui dirige l'alliance d'opposition, a dit de son côté dans un communiqué publié sur Facebook qu'il s'était retiré de Mekelle, et que le gouvernement régional serait "temporairement transféré hors de Mekelle et opérerait depuis un autre endroit".
Une source humanitaire et un habitant de Mekelle, sous couvert d'anonymat, ont confirmé que la ville était désormais aux mains des forces gouvernementales.
Le cabinet du Premier ministre Abiy Ahmed n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire.
La prise de Mekelle par les forces pro-gouvernementales constitue une importante perte pour l'alliance d'opposition dirigée par le TPLF, qui avait lancé une vaste [USN:L8N45F0T4 TEXT:"offensive"] le 23 septembre contre l'armée éthiopienne.
Les forces fédérales éthiopiennes et les combattants alliés ont lancé une contre-offensive rapide dans le Tigré, mais selon les analystes, ces combats — qui constituent la pire escalade depuis la guerre civile de 2020-2022 — risquent de dégénérer en un conflit régional plus vaste.
Le gouvernement fédéral d'Addis-Abeba a rompu ses relations diplomatiques avec l'Érythrée la semaine dernière, l'accusant de soutenir l'alliance rebelle aux côtés du Soudan et de l'Égypte. Les trois pays rejettent ces accusations.

items.title: Opec+ set to keep November oil output targets steady amid war disruptions
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: Gulf Opec+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran ...
items.body: Opec+ is set to keep oil production targets steady for November, three sources close to the matter said ahead of the group's meeting on Sunday. Gulf Opec+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran, with exports fluctuating at 60-80% of normal levels in recent months. The war has also delayed the group's output capacity review - crucial to determine members' 2027 output quotas - because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources have said. The Opec+ group, comprising the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia, has agreed in principle to keep targets steady for November, the three sources close to the talks said. Opec+ has been raising output targets for much of 2026 after years of production cuts, but most of the increases stayed on paper because of the Middle East conflict. The seven core Opec+ members pumped 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly 5 million bpd below prewar levels in February, Opec data shows. Opec+ still has about 2 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members. It needs a capacity review to decide how to distribute increases and any changes to output are unlikely before 2027, sources have said. The group's seven core members meeting on Sunday are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman.

items.title: Haunted by grief, Gaza's displaced still wait overseas for return
items.author: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
items.creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
items.summary: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.
items.body:
Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.
Hassayna is one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war that was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, and who remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures. They still mourn dead relatives and their [USN:L1N45F09E TEXT:"destroyed homes"] and neighbourhoods.
"I left Gaza and came to Egypt, the land of Kinana (referring to Egypt), but at the same time, this will not be forgotten, my dear brother, it will not be forgotten," he said.
"I am waiting for the opportunity, I am waiting for the moment when Gaza becomes stable so I can return to my country, and be a productive member of this country, and be a positive force for the country."
Nearly a year after a ceasefire in Gaza that was meant to start a process of reconstruction under a technocratic government along with a political process that would lead to an eventual full Israeli withdrawal, little has changed.
Israeli forces still hold more than 60% of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most of the area where Palestinians live, mostly in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies and no prospect of reconstruction soon.
Some 308 members of Hassayna's [USN:L8N4400Z0 TEXT:"extended family"] were killed when Israeli strikes destroyed a cluster of Gaza City apartment buildings where they had gathered for shelter on November 22, 2023, according to Palestinian authorities.
Among those killed were his wife, four of their adult sons and four small grandchildren including an infant only a few months old.
Hassayna's oldest son Mohammed is also in Cairo along with his own four children, as is the widow of one of his dead sons with her daughter. He has brothers in the Egyptian capital too.
One daughter was medically evacuated to Turkey with her husband and six children, and another daughter remains in Gaza with her five children although her husband was killed in the attack.
The Israeli military did not respond to a request for comment on the details of the November 22 strike. It said its attacks in Gaza are directed at military targets, while trying to reduce harm to civilians.
ABOUT 7,000 PALESTINIANS HAVE RETURNED TO GAZA In August, Hassayna watched on video from Cairo as relatives buried 112 family members, including his wife, sons and grandchildren, whose bodies had been recovered from the rubble, with dozens still missing.
Hassayna owned a business selling tools for firefighting and safety equipment in Gaza and some of his goods survived the war. He periodically sells some to fund his stay in Cairo, where he has remarried.
All those who left Gaza were vetted before their departure by both Israel and Egypt, but many have found it hard to return to the territory.
Although some Israeli politicians have urged a policy of encouraging all Gaza's population to leave and to prevent those who left from returning, about 7,000 have gone home. Hassayna believes Egypt will stop any widespread displacement of Palestinians from Gaza.
However, no widespread return of those who fled Gaza may be likely until the territory's prospects are clearer.
"If Gaza returns. If there is an international agreement (with) a comprehensive situation for the Palestinian people and construction begins, why would I delay?" he said.

items.body:
Andrius Sytas　Terje Solsvik

[リガ ４日 ロイター] - ラトビアで３日に実施された総選挙は、親ウクライナ・中道のクルベルグス首相率いる「連合リスト」が予想を上回る大差で勝利した。開票速報で明らかになった。ロシアによる攻撃の可能性に対する警戒が高まる中、多くの有権者が緊張感を抱えながら投票に臨んだ。

開票率８８％の時点で、連合リストの得票率は３６．６％。ポピュリスト政党「ラトビア・ファースト」 が１３．４％で続いた。

バルト諸国はこの数カ月、ロシアがウクライナ支援の切り崩しと社会不安の醸成を狙って、欧州各地で破壊工作やサイバー攻撃などのハイブリッド攻撃を仕掛けていると警告してきた。ロシア側は、こうした非難には根拠がないと反発している。

クルベルグス氏は３日夕、リガにある党本部で、「驚くほどよい結果だ。ここまでとは予想していなかった」と述べ、首相続投に意欲を示した。

開票速報によれば、単独過半数には達していないため、組閣には連立が必要となる。同氏は、ラトビア・ファーストとの連立は望まないと述べた。

親ロシアの「主権」は出口調査で得票率１１．６％で３位、ロシアに対する強硬路線を掲げる右派政党「国民連合」が９．１％だった。

クルベルグス氏は選挙戦で、対ドローン能力の強化や国防費を国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比５％に維持すると約束した。この水準はＮＡＴＯ加盟国の中でも最も高い部類に入る。ラトビア・ファーストは、国内のロシア系住民の支持取り込みを図った。

親ロシア政党は、ウクライナへの支援を全てやめて、特にロシア語を話す少数派の生活費の問題にもっと力を入れるべきだと主張した。
